I am about to depart,
and I look to the character of you all."
Minister Wén Zhǒng said:
"To internally manage the duties of borders and frontiers,
and externally prepare for farming and warfare.
Leaving no land uncultivated,
and ensuring the people are closely attached—
that is my task."
Minister Fàn Lǐ said:
"To assist a ruler in peril,
and preserve a state facing destruction.
Not shaming disgrace in hardship,
but calmly enduring in a humiliated position.
To go and surely return, avenging with the ruler—
that is my task."
Minister Kǔchéng said:
"To issue the ruler's commands,
and illuminate the ruler's virtue.
To share hardship in poverty,
and share hegemony in advancement.
To manage complexities and bring order to chaos,
making the people know their duties—
that is my task."
Minister Yì Yōng said:
"To receive orders and undertake missions,
forging alliances with the feudal lords.
To convey commands and achieve aims,
sending and receiving gifts.
To resolve worries and avert troubles,
ensuring there is no doubt.
To not forget commands when abroad,
and not incur blame when at home—
that is my task."
Minister Hào Jìn said:
"With one heart and unified will,
above, to be equal with all;
below, not to disobey orders.
Acting in accordance with the ruler's commands,
cultivating virtue and practicing righteousness,
keeping faith and honoring the past.
Facing errors and deciding doubts,
admonishing when the ruler errs.
With an upright heart unyielding,
presenting faults and arranging fairness.
Not favoring relatives,
nor showing partiality externally.
Devoting oneself to the ruler,
consistent from start to finish—
that is my task."
Minister Zhū Jī Yǐng said:
"To observe the enemy and set formations,
flying arrows and raising arms.
Treading on bellies and crossing corpses,
with blood flowing abundantly.
Greedy for advance, never retreating,
when two armies confront each other.
To defeat the enemy and attack the multitude,
intimidating all states—
that is my task."
Minister Gāo Rú said:
"To cultivate virtue and bestow kindness,
comforting and caring for the people.
Personally attending to worries and toils,
acting always with personal involvement.
Mourning the dead and caring for the sick,
saving and sustaining the people's lives.
Storing the old and reserving the new,
eating without varied flavors.
Enriching the state and solidifying the people,
nurturing tools for the ruler—
that is my task."
Minister Jì Ní said:
"To observe the heavens and examine the earth,
recording the calendar of yīn and yáng.
To watch changes and interpret disasters,
distinguishing between ominous and auspicious signs.
When the sun and moon bear colors,
and the five essences err in their courses,
to know fortune upon seeing auspicious signs,
and perceive calamity upon the emergence of evil—
that is my task."
The King of Yuè said:
"Though I enter the northern state,
becoming a destitute captive of Wú,
with you, the various ministers, embracing virtue and holding skills,
each guarding your duties,
to protect the altars of state,
what sorrow have I?"
Then they parted at the shore of the Zhè Jiāng,
the assembled ministers shedding tears,
all in mourning.
The King of Yuè looked up to heaven and sighed:
"Death—
is what people fear.
But as for I hearing of death,
in my heart there is no trepidation."
Then he boarded the boat and went straight away,
never looking back.
The King of Yuè's wife leaned on the boat and wept,
watching the crows pecking at shrimp on the river islets,
flying away and returning again.
Then, weeping, she sang:
"Look up at the flying birds, oh, the crows and kites,
soaring in the dark void, calling as they flutter.
Gathering on islets and shores, oh, so carefree,
pecking shrimp, raising wings, oh, among the clouds.
Going and coming, oh, as they please.
I, guiltless, oh, have failed the earth;
what wrong have I done, oh, that heaven condemns me?
Sailing alone, oh, westward bound,
who knows when, oh, I'll return!
My heart aching, oh, as if cut,
tears streaming, oh, in twin falls."
Then she lamented again:
"Those flying birds, oh, the kites and crows,
already wheel and soar, oh, gathering and reviving.
Their hearts fixed, oh, on plain shrimp,
why dwell and eat, oh, by rivers and lakes?
Hovering and soaring again, oh, drifting and fluttering,
leaving and returning again, oh, alas!
First serving my lord, oh, I left home;
ending my life, oh, at my lord's capital.
What fortune, oh, to finally meet this fate?
Leaving my state, oh, for Wú.
Wife in coarse cloth, oh, becomes a maid;
husband without crown, oh, becomes a slave.
Years stretch far, oh, hard to endure;
grief and bitter pain, oh, wrench my heart.
Bowels in a thousand knots, oh, burden my chest;
alas, the sorrow, oh, makes me forget food.
I wish my body, oh, were like a bird's,
body soaring, oh, with raised wings.
Leaving my state, oh, my heart wavers;
feelings indignant and grieved, oh, who understands!"
The King of Yuè heard his wife's mournful song,
his heart inwardly pained,
and said:
"Why should I sorrow?
My six wings are fully prepared!"
Thereupon he entered Wú.
Seeing Fū Chāi,
he kowtowed twice, paying homage as a subject,
saying:
"The lowly subject Gōu Jiàn of the Eastern Sea,
ashamed above to the august heaven,
and below to the earth.
Inadequate in strength and effort,
I have disgraced your army's officers,
and deserve punishment at the border.
Great King, you have pardoned my grave offense,
deigning to employ your subject,
to make him hold the broom and dustpan.
Truly, I receive your profound grace,
able to preserve my fleeting life—
overwhelmed with gratitude above and shame below.
Your subject Gōu Jiàn kowtows and bows his head."
King Fūchāi of Wú said:
"I have been at fault towards you,
but do you not remember the enmity of our former king?"
King of Yuè replied:
"If I die, then I die,
but I beg Your Majesty to pardon me."
Wǔ Xū stood nearby,
his eyes like blazing fire,
his voice like thunder,
and came forward saying:
"When flying birds are high in the blue clouds,
we still try to shoot them down with fine arrows attached to strings,
how much more when they rest nearby on our ornamental ponds,
or gather in our courtyard corridors?
Now the King of Yuè is exiled in the southern mountains,
wandering in uninhabitable lands,
yet he fortunately comes to tread upon our territory,
entering our prison gates.
This is like cooked meat ready for the kitchen,
how can we let it escape?"
The King of Wú said:
"I have heard that killing those who have surrendered
brings calamity upon three generations.
It is not that I spare Yuè out of affection,
but I fear the punishment of Heaven,
which instructs me to pardon him."
Grand Steward Pǐ advised:
"Zǐxū understands temporary tactics,
but not the way to secure a state.
I beg Your Majesty to follow your decision,
and not be constrained by the words of petty men."
Fūchāi thus did not execute the King of Yuè,
but ordered him to drive carriages and tend horses,
kept secluded within the palace.
After three months,
the King of Wú summoned the King of Yuè for an audience.
The King of Yuè prostrated himself in front,
while Fàn Lǐ stood behind him.
The King of Wú said to Fàn Lǐ:
"I have heard that chaste women do not marry into ruined families,
and benevolent worthies do not serve annihilated states.
Now the King of Yuè is without virtue,
his state nearly destroyed,
his altars of land and grain broken and fallen,
himself facing death and the end of his line,
laughed at by all under heaven.
Yet you and your lord have become slaves,
coming to submit to Wú.
Is this not base!
I wish to pardon your crime,
if you can change your heart and reform yourself,
abandoning Yuè to join Wú?"
Fàn Lǐ replied:
"I have heard that ministers of a destroyed state dare not discuss governance,
and generals of a defeated army dare not speak of courage.
I was neither loyal nor trustworthy in Yuè,
and now the King of Yuè, not obeying Your Majesty's commands,
raised troops to resist you,
thus incurring this punishment.
Both ruler and minister have surrendered,
and through Your Majesty's great kindness,
we are able to preserve ourselves.
I only wish to serve sweeping and cleaning duties inside,
and run errands outside -
this is my desire."
At this, the King of Yuè lay prostrate weeping,
thinking he had lost Fàn Lǐ.
The King of Wú, knowing Fàn Lǐ could not be made his minister,
said to him:
"Since you will not change your resolve,
I shall place you again in the stone chamber."
Fàn Lǐ said:
"I beg to obey your command."
The King of Wú rose and entered his palace,
while the King of Yuè and Fàn Lǐ hurried into the stone chamber.
The King of Yuè wore short breeches,
and a woodcutter's headcloth.
His wife wore an unhemmed skirt,
and a jacket fastened on the left.
The husband chopped fodder and tended horses,
while the wife fetched water, removed manure, and swept.
For three years they showed no anger,
nor any resentment on their faces.
The King of Wú climbed a high tower,
and saw the King of Yuè with his wife and Fàn Lǐ sitting beside the horse manure,
yet maintaining the etiquette between ruler and minister,
and preserving the decorum between husband and wife.
The king turned to Grand Steward Pǐ saying:
"That King of Yuè
is a man of integrity.
Fàn Lǐ
is a scholar of principle.
Though in dire straits,
they do not abandon the rites between ruler and minister.
I pity them."
Grand Steward Pǐ said:
"I beg Your Majesty, with a sage's heart,
to take pity on these poor, isolated men."
The King of Wú said:
"For your sake, I shall pardon them."
Three months later,
he chose an auspicious day to pardon them.
Summoning Grand Steward Pǐ to consult, he said:
"Yuè and Wú
share the same land with connected borders.
Gōu Jiàn, foolish and crafty,
personally sought to harm us.
I, receiving the divine spirits of Heaven,
and the accumulated virtue of former kings,
punished the Yuè invaders,
imprisoning them in the stone chamber.
My heart cannot bear to see this,
and I wish to pardon them.
What do you think?"
Grand Steward Pǐ said:
"I have heard that no virtue goes unrewarded.
If Your Majesty bestows benevolent kindness upon Yuè,
how would Yuè dare not repay it?
I beg Your Majesty to carry out your intention."
Hearing this, the King of Yuè
summoned Fàn Lǐ and told him:
"I have heard news from outside,
and my heart is secretly joyful,
yet I fear it may not come to pass."
Fàn Lǐ said:
"Your Majesty, set your mind at ease.
Events will unfold as destined,
first at the Jade Gate.
This year, on the wùyín day of the twelfth month,
at the hour of sunrise.
Wù
is a day of imprisonment.
Yín
is the hour following darkness.
It coincides with the gēngchén year's subsequent meeting.
To hear joyful news on a wùyín day
without being punished for one's crimes
is due to the day.
The hour of mǎo conflicts with wù,
the merit officer becomes the soaring snake approaching wù,
while planning profitable matters rests with the azure dragon.
The azure dragon
triumphs first.
But approaching yǒu,
it becomes the breath of death.
And overcoming yín,
this means the hour overcomes the day,
with additional assistance,
so the matters sought
will bring worries above and below.
Is this not the heaven's net spread wide,
where all things suffer injury?
Why should Your Majesty rejoice?"
Sure enough, Wǔ Zǐxū admonished the King of Wú:
"In former times, Jié imprisoned Tāng but did not kill him,
and Zhòu imprisoned King Wén but did not slay him.
Heaven's way turns around,
transforming calamity into blessing.
Thus Xià was destroyed by Tāng,
and Yīn was annihilated by Zhōu.
Now that Your Majesty has imprisoned the Lord of Yuè without executing him,
I consider Your Majesty deeply deluded.
Will you not incur the troubles of Xià and Yīn?"
The King of Wú then summoned the King of Yuè,
but did not see him for a long time.
Fàn Lǐ and Wén Zhǒng worried and divined, saying:
"The King of Wú is going to detain him."
After a while,
Grand Steward Pǐ came out,
met with Senior Official Zhǒng and Fàn Lǐ, and said the King of Yuè was again confined in the stone chamber.
Wǔ Zǐxū again admonished the King of Wú:
"I have heard that when a king attacks an enemy state,
upon victory he executes them,
thus avoiding future worries of revenge,
and sparing his descendants from trouble.
Now the King of Yuè has entered the stone chamber,
you should quickly deal with him,
or he will surely become Wú's calamity."
Grand Steward Pǐ said:
"In former times, Duke Huán of Qí ceded to Duke of Yān the territory his army had reached,
and the ruler of Qí gained a reputation for virtue.
Duke Xiāng of Sòng waited to cross the river before battle,
and the Spring and Autumn Annals praised his righteousness.
Thus he established merit and gained fame,
and though his army was defeated, his virtue remained.
If Your Majesty truly pardons the King of Yuè,
your achievement will surpass the Five Hegemons,
and your name will exceed the ancients."
The King of Wú said:
"Wait until my illness improves,
then I will pardon him for you, Grand Steward."
One month later,
the King of Yuè left the stone chamber,
and summoned Fàn Lǐ, saying:
"The King of Wú is ill,
and has not recovered for three months.
I have heard that according to the way of ministers,
when the ruler is ill, the minister should worry.
Moreover, the King of Wú has treated me
with great kindness."
The illness shows no sign of recovery,
so I ask you to divine it."
Fàn Lǐ said:
"The King of Wú will not die,
that is clear.
By the jǐsì day,
he should recover.
I beg Your Majesty to consider this."
The King of Yuè said:
"The reason I endure hardship and do not die,
is solely due to your strategies.
If I hesitate midway,
how could that be my resolve!
Whether it can be done or not,
I rely on your planning."
Fàn Lǐ said:
"I privately observe that the King of Wú is truly inhuman,
often speaking of the righteousness of King Táng but not practicing it.
I wish Your Majesty to request to inquire about his illness,
and if you gain an audience,
then seek to taste his stool,
observe his complexion,
and then offer congratulations.
Say that he will not die,
predicting the recovery date.
Once your words prove true later,
then what has Your Majesty to worry about."
The next day, the King of Yuè said to Grand Steward Pǐ:
"This prisoner wishes to see him once to inquire about his illness."
Grand Steward Pǐ immediately entered and reported to the King of Wú,
who summoned and received him.
It happened that the King of Wú had just relieved himself,
and Grand Steward Pǐ was carrying out the foul waste,
when he met at the door,
the King of Yuè bowed,
requested to taste the king's waste,
to determine fortune or misfortune.
He then took the excrement with his hand and tasted it.
Upon entering, he said:
"The lower prisoner Gōu Jiàn congratulates Your Majesty,
your illness will recover by the jǐsì day,
and by the third month on the rénshēn day, you will be cured."
The King of Wú said:
"How do you know this?"
The King of Yuè said:
"Your servant once studied under a teacher who heard about stool:
if it follows the grain's taste but opposes the seasonal qi, it means death;
if it follows the seasonal qi, it means life.
Now,
I have privately tasted Your Majesty's stool,
its foul taste is bitter and sour like chǔ.
This taste
corresponds to the qi of spring and summer,
thus I know it."
The King of Wú was greatly pleased,
and said:
"A benevolent man."
He then pardoned the King of Yuè, allowing him to leave the stone chamber,
return to his palace,
and resume his duties of tending and herding as before.
After the King of Yuè tasted the foul waste,
he developed bad breath,
so Fàn Lǐ ordered his attendants all to eat cén grass,
to mask the odor.
Afterwards,
the King of Wú recovered from his illness on the day predicted by the King of Yuè,
and in his heart, he remembered his loyalty.
When he resumed governance,
he held a grand feast at Wéntái.
The King of Wú decreed:
"Today, prepare a seat facing north for the King of Yuè,
and all ministers shall treat him with the rites of a guest."
Wǔ Zǐxū hurried out,
went to his residence,
and did not attend the feast.
When the wine was flowing freely,
Grand Steward Pǐ said:
"How unusual!
Those seated here today,
each have their words.
The unbenevolent flee,
the benevolent remain.
I have heard:
those with the same voice harmonize,
those with the same heart seek each other.
Now the State Minister is a man of rigid courage;
perhaps he is inwardly ashamed of the presence of ultimate benevolence,
and thus does not attend the feast.
Could this be the reason?"
The King of Wú said:
"Indeed."
Thereupon Fàn Lǐ and the King of Yuè stood up together,
to offer a toast to the King of Wú,
their words were:
"Your servant Gōu Jiàn, along with minor official Fàn Lǐ,
raise our cups to offer a thousand-year longevity.
We say:
The sovereign above,
his commands illuminate the four seasons below,
and with whole heart, he examines the compassionate and benevolent.
Your Majesty personally bestows great grace,
establishes righteousness and practices benevolence,
with nine virtues and four barriers,
awing and subduing all ministers.
Oh, how splendid!
May your virtue be transmitted boundlessly,
reaching up to stir the sun,
bringing down auspicious signs in abundance.
May Your Majesty live ten thousand years,
long preserving the state of Wú.
May all within the four seas submit,
and the feudal lords pay tribute.
With the cup of wine raised,
may you forever receive myriad blessings."
Thereupon, the King of Wú was greatly pleased.
The next day,
Wǔ Zǐxū entered to admonish, saying:
"What did Your Majesty witness yesterday?
I have heard that those who harbor the heart of a tiger or wolf inwardly,
but outwardly hold fair speeches,
only use external appearances to preserve themselves.
A jackal cannot be called honest,
a wolf cannot be trusted.
Now Your Majesty is fond of listening to momentary flattery,
without considering the calamities of ten thousand years.
You abandon loyal and straightforward words,
and heed the talk of slanderers.
You do not eradicate the blood-dripping enmity,
nor cut off the poison-holding resentment.
It is like releasing a hair over a burning brazier, hoping it won't singe,
or throwing an egg from a great height, expecting it to remain whole.
Is that not perilous?
I have heard that Jié, ascending high, knew his danger,
yet did not know how to secure himself;
facing a blade, he knew death was near,
but did not know how to preserve himself.
The deluded who realize their error can turn back,
for the lost path is not far.
I beg Your Majesty to consider this."
The King of Wú said:
"I have been ill for three months,
yet never heard a single word from the Chancellor,
this shows the Chancellor's lack of compassion.
Nor did you offer what my mouth craves,
your heart showed no concern,
this shows the Chancellor's lack of benevolence.
As a minister, being neither benevolent nor compassionate,
how can one be considered loyal and trustworthy?
The King of Yuè, confused and lost,
abandoned his duty of guarding the borders,
personally led his ministers and people,
to come and submit to me,
this is his righteousness.
He personally became a prisoner,
his wife personally became a servant,
and he bears no grudge against me;
when I was ill,
he personally tasted my waste,
this is his compassion.
He emptied his treasury,
exhausted his treasures and coins,
without regard for his past,
this is his loyalty and trustworthiness.
With these three virtues established,
he supports me.
If I had listened to the Chancellor and executed him,
that would have been my lack of wisdom,
and only satisfied the Chancellor's personal wishes!
Would that not betray the August Heaven?"
Zǐxū said:
"Why does Your Majesty's speech turn things upside down?
When a tiger lowers its posture,
it is planning to strike.
When a fox crouches low,
it is seeking to capture.
A pheasant is caught in the net due to its dazzled movement,
a fish dies by the bait because of its delight.
Moreover, when Your Majesty first assumed governance,
you bore the ninth of the Jade Gate,
heeding warnings to avoid failure,
and had no faults.
This year on the jiǎxū day of the third month,
at the hour of the rooster's crow.
Jiǎxū
is the conjunction of the year's position.
The Green Dragon is in yǒu,
Virtue is in earth,
Punishment is in metal,
on this day, it harms the Virtue.
It indicates that a father will have a disobedient son,
a ruler will have a minister who defies authority.
Your Majesty considers the King of Yuè's submission to Wú as righteousness,
his drinking waste and eating foulness as compassion,
his emptying the treasury as benevolence.
Therefore, he has no love for others,
and cannot be trusted.
He listens and observes superficially,
only to preserve himself.
Now the King of Yuè serves as a minister in Wú,
this is his deep scheme.
He emptied his treasury,
yet showed no sign of resentment,
which is deceiving our king.
To drink the king's filth below
is to devour the king's heart above.
To taste the king's foulness below
is to consume the king's liver above.
How profound!
The King of Yuè's reverence for Wú
will lead to Wú's capture.
I beg Your Majesty to consider this carefully,
I dare not flee death and betray the former king.
Once the state lies in ruins,
and ancestral temples are overgrown with thorns,
can regret undo it?"
The King of Wú said:
"Set this aside, Chancellor,
speak no more of it,
I cannot bear to hear again."
Thereupon,
he pardoned the King of Yuè and sent him back to his country,
escorting him beyond Shémén.
The ministers bid him farewell.
The King of Wú said:
"I have pardoned you,
allowing your return to your country.
You must remember this grace from start to end,
may you strive diligently."
The King of Yuè bowed deeply and said:
"Now that Your Majesty pities my isolation and hardship,
granting me life and return to my country,
I, along with followers like Wén Zhǒng and Fàn Lǐ,
wish to die in your service.
By the vast heavens above,
I dare not betray you."
The King of Wú said:
"Alas!
I hear a nobleman does not repeat his words,
it is already decided,
may you strive diligently."
The King of Yuè bowed again and knelt prostrate,
then the King of Wú led him to his carriage,
with Fàn Lǐ holding the reins,
and they departed.
Upon reaching Sānjīn,
he looked up to the sky and sighed:
"Alas!
In my dire straits,
who would have thought I'd cross this ford again alive?"
He said to Fàn Lǐ:
"Today, the third month, jiǎchén day,
at the dié hour,
I, humble as I am, under heaven's mandate,
return to my homeland.
Might there be future troubles?"
Fàn Lǐ replied:
"Do not doubt, Great King,
but proceed straight on the path.
Yuè shall have fortune,
while Wú faces sorrow."
When they reached the banks of the Zhèjiāng River,
gazing upon the majestic beauty of Dàyuè's mountains and rivers,
the world seemed clear and renewed.
The king and his夫人 sighed:
"We had lost all hope,
bid eternal farewell to the people.
Who would have imagined returning,
revisiting our homeland?"
With these words, they covered their faces,
tears streaming down.
At this moment, all the people rejoiced,
and the ministers offered their congratulations.
King Gōu Jiàn of Yuè served Wú as a vassal,
until his return to Yuè,
which was in the seventh year of Gōu Jiàn's reign.
The common people bowed to him along the road,
saying:
"Our king, may you be free from hardship.
Now you have received heaven's blessings,
returning to the state of Yuè,
where the path of a hegemon shall rise from this moment."
The king replied:
"I was not cautious in heeding heaven's teachings,
and have no virtue towards the people.
Now I trouble the multitude to gather at the crossroads,
what virtue and transformation can I offer to repay the nation?"
He turned to Fàn Lǐ and said:
"Today is the day of Jǐsì in the twelfth month,
at the hour of mid-morning,
I wish to proceed to the capital at this time,
what do you think?"
Fàn Lǐ said:
"Your Majesty should wait a moment,
allow me to divine the day."
Thereupon Fàn Lǐ advanced and said:[25"How extraordinary!
Your Majesty's choice of day.
You should hasten quickly,
with chariots speeding and people running."
The King of Yuè whipped his horse and flew in his carriage,
thus returning to the palace.
Wú granted Yuè a territory of a hundred lǐ,
east to Tàndú,
west to Zhōuzōng,
south reaching the mountains,
north bordering the sea.
The King of Yuè said to Fàn Lǐ:
"I have suffered disgrace for years,
in circumstances enough to die,
but obtained your strategies, Prime Minister,
to return again to the southern land.
Now I wish to stabilize the state and build a city,
but the people are insufficient,
the work cannot be undertaken,
what should be done about this?"
Fàn Lǐ replied:
"Táng and Yú divined for land,
Xià and Yīn enfeoffed states,
the Ancient Duke constructed a city,
Zhōu's Luòyì subdued ten thousand lǐ,
its virtue reached the eight extremes,
was it merely to defeat strong enemies and conquer neighboring states?"
The King of Yuè said:
"I cannot continue the institutions of previous rulers,
cultivate virtue and maintain defense,
but lost the masses and dwelt on Kuàijī Mountain,
pleading for life and begging favor,
suffering humiliation and shame,
imprisoned in the Wú palace.
Fortunately, I have returned to my state,
restricted to a hundred lǐ fief.
I intend to honor the intentions of former rulers,
again reside above Kuàijī,
and should abandon the land of Wú."
Fàn Lǐ said:
"Formerly, Gōng Liú left Tái and his virtue was renowned in Xià,
Dǎnfù yielded land and his fame arose from Qí.
Now Your Majesty wishes to establish a capital for the state,
annexing the territory of enemy states,
if not situated in a accessible capital,
occupying a place reaching in four directions,
how will you establish the enterprise of a hegemon?"
The King of Yuè said:
"My plan is not yet decided,
I wish to build inner and outer city walls,
divide and establish neighborhoods,
and entrust this to the Prime Minister."
Thereupon Fàn Lǐ observed the celestial patterns,
modeling them after the Purple Palace,
and constructed a small city.
Its circumference was one thousand one hundred twenty-one paces,
one circle and three sides.
In the northwest, he erected the Dragon Flying Wings Tower,
to symbolize the Gate of Heaven.
In the southeast, he installed hidden drains and stone conduits,
to symbolize the Door of Earth.
The mound gate extended in four directions,
to symbolize the eight winds.
The outer wall was built with a gap in the northwest,
to show service to Wú,
not daring to block it.
Internally, to conquer Wú,
therefore leaving the northwest open,
unknown to Wú.
Facing north to acknowledge vassalage,
submitting fate to Wú.
Left and right positions exchanged,
not attaining their proper places,
clarifying subordinate status.
When the city was completed,
a strange mountain spontaneously appeared,
which was the Lángyá Dōngwǔ Mountain from the sea.
It came of itself in one night,
hence named Strange Mountain.
Fàn Lǐ said:
"In my construction of the city,
it corresponds to heaven.
The image of Kūnlún is preserved therein."
The King of Yuè said:
"I have heard that Kūnlún Mountain is the pillar of the earth,
bearing the august heaven above,
breathing energy throughout the cosmos,
resting on the earth below,
receiving all without exclusion,
nourishing sages and generating spirits,
cultivating and gathering emperors.
Thus emperors dwell on its southern slopes,
and the three sovereigns reside in its central lands.
My state,
cramped in heaven and earth's corner,
riding the southeastern dimension,
the Dipper far from the northern pole,
if not a city of dung and soil,
how can it compare in prosperity with royal states?"
Fàn Lǐ said:
"You only see the exterior,
not the interior.
I received the heavenly gate's model to construct the city,
combining energy with the earth,
mountain images already arranged,
hence Kūnlún emerged,
for Yuè's hegemony."
The King of Yuè said:
"If it is as the Prime Minister says,
it is my destiny."
Fàn Lǐ said:[136"Heaven and earth finally named it,
to manifest its reality,
called Dōngwǔ.
He built a roaming terrace atop it,
with a Minister of War gate to the southeast,
erecting a towering pavilion crowning the mountain peak,
as a spiritual terrace."
He built a detached palace at Huáiyáng,
the Midnight Terrace at Gāopíng,
the Chariot Terrace at Chéngqiū,
established a park at Lèyě,
the Feasting Terrace at Shíshì,
the Fasting Terrace at Jìshān.
When Gōu Jiàn traveled,
he rested and dined at the Ice Kitchen.
The King of Yuè then summoned Prime Minister Fàn Lǐ, Minister Wén Zhǒng, and Minister Yǐng,
asking:
"I wish today to ascend the Bright Hall and oversee state affairs,
concentrating kindness and issuing decrees,
to comfort the people.
On what day may this be done?
I rely on the three sages to maintain order."
Fàn Lǐ said:
"Today,
is a Bǐngwǔ day.
Bǐng,
is the masculine leader,
this day is auspicious.
Moreover, with this fine hour,
I humbly believe we can have a beginning without end,
attaining the center of heaven and earth."
Minister Wén Zhǒng said:
"The front carriage has already overturned,
the rear carriage must be cautious,
I hope the king will deeply consider this."
Fàn Lǐ said:[172"This gentleman indeed seldom sees such.
Our king now renews governance on Bǐngwǔ day,
rescuing its foundation,
this is the first appropriateness.
Metal controls the beginning,
and fire rescues its end,
this is the second appropriateness.
The worry of accumulating metal,
turns to involve water,
this is the third appropriateness.
Ruler and minister have distinctions,
not losing their principles,
this is the fourth appropriateness.
King and ministers arise together,
the world is established,
this is the fifth appropriateness.
I urge haste to ascend the Bright Hall and govern."
The King of Yuè began his governance that day,
cautious and careful,
not extravagant in public,
not wasteful in private.
The King of Yuè contemplated revenge against Wú,
not just for a day.
He tormented his body and labored his mind,
continuing day into night.
When sleepy, he irritated his eyes with smartweed,
when feet were cold, he soaked them in water.
In winter, he often embraced ice,
in summer, he still held fire.
With a heart full of sorrow and a will steeped in bitterness,
he hung a gall bladder by his door,
tasting it upon entering and exiting,
never ceasing to speak of it.
In the dead of night, he secretly wept,
and after weeping, he would let out long sighs.
King Yuè said:
"The King of Wú enjoys fine clothing close to his body;
I wish to gather kudzu,
have the weaving women craft fine cloth from it to present to him,
hoping to win the heart of the King of Wú.
What do you think of this?"
The ministers replied:
"Excellent."
So he sent men and women of the state into the mountains to gather kudzu,
to make yellow silk cloth,
intending to offer it.
Before an envoy could be dispatched,
the King of Wú heard that the King of Yuè was devoted to self-restraint,
eating without varied flavors,
wearing without colorful silks,
and though he had the means to tour five terraces,
he never spent a day in leisurely enjoyment.
"I wish to send him a letter in recognition,
and increase his fiefdom."
Extending east to Gōuyǒng,
west to Zuìlǐ,
south to Gūmò,
and north to Píngyuán,
spanning over eight hundred li in breadth.

The King of Yuè then sent his minister Wén Zhǒng to procure a hundred thousand bolts of kudzu cloth, nine dǎng of sweet honey, seven ornate boxes, five pairs of fox fur, and ten bundles of Jìn bamboo,
as a return gift for the enfeoffment.
The King of Wú received them and said:
"I thought Yuè, a remote and rustic state, had no treasures;
yet now they present these tribute goods in return for the ritual,
this shows Yuè's cautious mindfulness and gratitude,
not forgetting the favor of Wú.
Originally, Yuè was a thriving state of a thousand li;
though I enfeoffed them,
I did not cover their entire territory."
Zǐxū heard of this,
retired to his quarters to lie down,
and said to his attendants:
"Our lord has forgotten the prisoner in the stone chamber,
released into the southern forests;
now he merely wanders the wilds with tigers and leopards and the grasses beyond the wastes.
In my heart,
is there no harm in this?"
The King of Wú, upon receiving the offering of kudzu cloth,
further increased Yuè's fiefdom,
bestowing feathered ornaments, ceremonial staffs, and robes of a feudal lord.
The state of Yuè was greatly pleased;
the women gathering kudzu, moved by the King of Yuè's arduous efforts,
composed a poem of hardship, saying:
"Kudzu vines stretch unbroken, lush and dense,
our lord's heart suffers, yet fate changes it.
Tasting gall not bitter, sweet as syrup,
bids us gather kudzu to weave into silk.
Weaving women toil, not daring delay.
Finer than gauze, light as mist,
named fine plain cloth, to be offered up.
The King of Yuè rejoices, guilt forgotten and pardoned,
the King of Wú delights, sending swift missives.
Enfeoffment enlarged, lands increased, bestowed with rare feathers,
staffs and mats, the regalia of lords.
Ministers bow and dance, the sovereign's face eased,
what worry can our king not shift!"
Thereupon,
the King of Yuè cultivated virtue within,
spread his principles abroad,
the ruler did not dictate teachings,
ministers did not claim strategies,
the people were not commanded,
officials did not name duties.
The state was serene and orderly,
with no need for decrees.
The King of Yuè filled the treasuries,
cultivated the fields,
enriching the people and strengthening the state,
all secure and the way prosperous.
The King of Yuè then took eight ministers and four friends as mentors,
consulting them on governance from time to time.
Minister Wén Zhǒng said:
"It is simply about loving the people."
The King of Yuè asked:
"How so?"
Zhǒng replied:
"Benefit them without harm,
help them succeed without failure,
let them live without killing,
give to them without taking away."
The King of Yuè said:
"I wish to hear more."
Zhǒng said:
"Do not take what the people cherish—that benefits them.
Let the people not miss their seasons—that ensures success.
Reduce penalties and punishments—that preserves life.
Lighten taxes and levies—that gives to them.
Do not build many terraces for leisure—that brings them joy.
Keep peace without harshness—that pleases them.
If the people lose what they cherish, it harms them.
If farmers miss their seasons, it ruins them.
If crimes are not pardoned, it kills them.
If taxes are heavy and levies harsh, it takes from them.
Building many terraces and exhausting the people—that torments them.
Forcing labor and disturbing the people—that angers them.
I have heard that those skilled in ruling treat the people as parents love their children,
as elder brothers love their younger siblings;
hearing of their hunger and cold, they grieve;
seeing their toil and hardship, they sorrow."
The King of Yuè then relaxed punishments and reduced penalties,
and lessened taxes and levies.
Thereupon,
the people became prosperous and wealthy,
all possessing the courage of armored warriors.
In the ninth year,
in the first month,
the King of Yuè summoned his five senior ministers and told them:
"In the past,
Yuè abandoned its ancestral temples,
I became a destitute captive,
shamed before all under heaven,
humiliated among the feudal lords.
Now, I think of Wú
as a lame man does not forget walking,
a blind man does not forget seeing.
I lack a strategy;
I rely on your counsel."
Fú Tóng said:
"In the past, the fall of the state and the wandering people were known throughout the land.
Now, if we have a plan,
we should not reveal it prematurely.
I have heard that when birds are about to strike,
they first crouch low.
When fierce beasts are about to attack,
they surely smooth their fur and lie still.
When birds of prey are about to seize,
they fly low and fold their wings.
When a sage is about to act,
he must speak humbly and harmonize with the masses.
The plans of a sage
cannot be seen in form,
nor can their true intent be known.
Strike when the moment comes,
so that there are no swift, fault-finding troops ahead,
and no ambushes lying in wait behind.
Now, as Your Majesty faces the enemy to defeat Wú,
you should use modest words,
and not let them leak out.
I have heard that the King of Wú has armies stronger than Qí and Jìn,
yet has deep enmity with Chǔ.
Your Majesty should ally closely with Qí,
forge strong ties with Jìn,
secretly secure relations with Chǔ,
and diligently serve Wú.
Wú's ambition is fierce, arrogant, and self-praising;
it will surely belittle the feudal lords and bully neighboring states.
When these three states contend for power,
they will turn into hostile states,
inevitably clashing and fighting.
Yuè can take advantage of their weakness,
attack them then,
and overcome them.
Even the armies of the Five Emperors
could not surpass this strategy."
Fàn Lǐ said:
"I have heard that in planning to conquer an enemy state,
one must observe the omens of action.
At the assembly at Mèngjīn,
the feudal lords said it was feasible,
yet King Wǔ declined.
Now, Wú and Chǔ are locked in hatred,
their enmity unresolved.
Though Qí is not close,
it outwardly provides aid.
Though Jìn does not align,
it still upholds its righteousness.
When ministers within devise plans and settle on strategies against enemies,
and neighboring states communicate without cutting off support,
this is precisely when Wú rises to hegemony,
and the feudal lords pay it highest respect.
I have heard that the lofty collapse,
the lush-leaved are broken.
At noon, the sun must shift."
The moon waxes only to wane.
The four seasons do not flourish simultaneously,
the five elements do not race together.
Yīn and yáng alternate in dominance,
for energy has its peaks and declines.
Thus, overflowing dike waters
do not surpass their measure,
and smoldering dying flames
do not regain their blaze.
When water is calm, there is no fury of swirling eddies;
when fire diminishes, there is no heat to singe hair.
Now Wú rides on the might of the feudal lords
to issue commands across the realm,
unaware that its virtue is meager and grace shallow,
its path narrow and resentment widespread,
its authority precarious and wisdom fading,
its strength exhausted and prestige broken,
its troops blunted and army retreating,
its officers scattered and masses dissolved.
I urge you to marshal the forces and整顿军队,
await their collapse,
then strike in their wake.
With blades unstained by blood,
and soldiers not needing to pivot their heels,
the sovereign and ministers of Wú will be captured.
I hope Your Majesty will conceal your presence,
revealing no movement,
to observe their stillness. 」
Grand Master Kǔchéng said:
「Water can buoy plants and trees,
yet also sink them.
Earth can nurture all things,
yet also kill them.
Rivers and seas can lower streams and valleys,
yet also receive their tribute.
The sage can follow the multitude,
yet also command them.
Now Wú inherits Hélǘ's military system and Zǐxū's institutional teachings,
with governance stable and unimpaired,
victorious in battle and undefeated.
Grand Master Pǐ,
a reckless and flattering man,
is shrewd in strategy,
but negligent in court affairs.
Zǐxū strove in warfare,
and died for his remonstrations.
With these two holding power,
disruption is inevitable.
I hope the king will humble his heart and conceal himself,
revealing no plans or schemes,
then Wú can be destroyed. 」
Grand Master Hào said:
「Now the ruler of Wú is arrogant and his ministers extravagant,
the people well-fed and the army bold,
facing external enemies encroaching on their borders,
and internal tremors from contending ministers,
making them vulnerable to attack. 」
Grand Master Gōurú said:
「Heaven has four seasons,
humans have five conquests.
In the past, Tāng and Wǔ leveraged the advantage of the four seasons to subdue Xià and Yīn,
while Huán and Mù capitalized on the convenience of the five conquests to align the six states.
This is seizing the moment to triumph. 」
The king said:
「Without the advantage of the four seasons or the convenience of the five conquests,
I hope each of you will attend to your duties. 」
In the second month of the tenth year of King Gōu Jiàn of Yuè,
the King pondered deeply and contemplated far,
recalling the humiliation suffered from Wú,
and by the blessings of divine favor,
had regained the state of Yuè.
His ministers offered guidance,
each proposing strategies,
their words aligned and intentions united.
Gōu Jiàn respectfully followed,
and his state grew prosperous.
Five years after returning to Yuè,
he had yet to hear of any friends willing to die for the cause.
Some said the officials cherished their own lives,
and treasured their bodies.
So he ascended the Jiàn Tower,
observing to see if his ministers showed any signs of concern.
Chancellor Fàn Lǐ, Minister Wén Zhǒng, Gōu Rú, and others sat solemnly in rows,
though harboring worries,
they did not show it in their expressions.
King Yuè then struck the bell, sounded the alarm, and summoned his ministers,
making a covenant with them:
"I have suffered disgrace and humiliation,
ashamed before the Zhōu King above,
and embarrassed before Jìn and Chǔ below.
Fortunately, through the strategies of you ministers,
I have returned to the state, reformed governance,
enriched the people, and nurtured the scholars.
Yet in five years, I have not heard of any scholars willing to die or ministers seeking to avenge the shame.
How then can we achieve merit?"
The ministers remained silent, none responding.
King Yuè looked up to the sky and sighed:
"I have heard that when the ruler worries, the ministers feel disgraced;
when the ruler is disgraced, the ministers should die.
Now I personally endured the hardship of enslavement,
suffered the shame of captivity and defeat,
unable to assist myself,
I must rely on the virtuous and appoint the benevolent,
only then can we attack Wú.
Heavily burdening you ministers,
why are you so easy to see but difficult to employ?"
At this,
Jì Náo, young and of low rank,
seated at the back,
raised his hand and hurried forth,
stepping forward on the mat to say:
"How mistaken are the king's words!
It is not that the ministers are easy to see but hard to employ;
it is that the king does not know how to employ them."
King Yuè said:
"What do you mean?"
Jì Náo replied:
"Official positions, wealth, coins, and gold rewards—
these are what the ruler considers light;
grasping blades, treading on edges, sacrificing lives, and facing death—
these are what scholars value heavily.
Now the king readily offers what he considers light,
yet demands what scholars value heavily.
How perilous this is!"
Then King Yuè fell silent, displeased,
his face showing shame,
and he dismissed the ministers,
approaching Jì Náo to ask:
"What must I do to win the hearts of the scholars?"
Jì Náo answered:
"For a ruler to honor benevolence and righteousness—
this is the gate to governance.
The scholars and people—
they are the roots of the ruler.
To open the gate and secure the roots,
nothing is better than rectifying oneself.
The way to rectify oneself
is to be cautious with one's attendants.
The attendants—
they are the cause of the ruler's rise and fall.
I hope the king will wisely select his attendants,
seeking only the worthy.
In the past, Tài Gōng, with just nine sounds enough,
was a starving man at Pán Xī,
yet Xī Bó employed him and became king.
Guǎn Zhòng,
a fugitive prisoner from Lǔ,
bore the slander of greed,
yet Qí Huán obtained him and became hegemon.
Thus the tradition says:
Lose the scholars, and you perish.
Gain the scholars, and you thrive.
If the king is careful with his attendants,
why worry that the ministers cannot be employed?"
King Yuè said:
"I employ the worthy and appoint the capable,
each with distinct duties.
I humbly hold high hopes,
longing to hear plans for revenge.
Yet now they all hide their voices and conceal their forms,
I do not hear their words.
Where does the fault lie?"
Jì Náo said:
"Selecting the worthy and testing them in practice—
each has its level.
Send them on difficult distant missions
to test their sincerity.
Confide in them secretly
to know their trustworthiness.
Discuss affairs with them
to observe their wisdom.
Give them wine to drink
to see if they become disorderly.
Assign them tasks
to examine their ability.
Show them beauties
to distinguish their demeanor.
With these five methods set,
scholars will reveal their true nature,
and people will exhaust their wisdom.
Knowing their wisdom is fully expressed and truth shown,
then what worries remain for ruler and ministers?"
King Yuè said:
"I employ strategists to test their substance,
and people exhaust their wisdom,
yet some scholars have not fully presented words beneficial to me."
Jì Náo said:
"Fàn Lǐ is perceptive and understands internal affairs;
Wén Zhǒng has foresight and sees external matters.
I hope the king will invite Minister Zhǒng to deeply discuss,
and the path to hegemony will be at hand."
King Yuè then invited Minister Zhǒng and asked:
"In the past, I received your guidance,
and saved myself from dire straits.
Now I wish to adopt an unconstrained plan
to avenge my long-standing enemy.
What action will bring success?"
Minister Zhǒng said:
"I have heard that high-flying birds die for delicious food,
deep-spring fish die for fragrant bait.
Now to attack Wú,
we must first seek what they love,
understand their desires,
then we can grasp their reality."
King Yuè said:
"What people love,
even if it's their desire,
how can it be used to ensure their death?"
Minister Zhǒng said:
"To repay grievance, revenge shame, crush Wú, and destroy the enemy—
there are nine methods.
May the king examine them."
King Yuè said:
"I have suffered disgrace and harbor worries,
ashamed inwardly before court ministers,
embarrassed outwardly before the various lords,
my heart confused,
my spirit empty.
Even with nine methods,
how can I understand them?"
Minister Zhǒng said:
"These nine methods—
Tāng and Wén obtained them and became kings,
Huán and Mù obtained them and became hegemons.
Attacking cities and capturing towns
became as easy as shedding sandals.
I hope the king will peruse them."
Zhǒng said:
"First: revere heaven and serve ghosts,
to seek their blessings.
Second: value wealth and coins to gift their ruler,
offer abundant goods and bribes to please his ministers.
Third: inflate the price of grain and fodder to empty their state,
indulge their desires to exhaust their people.
Fourth: send beautiful women to delude his mind,
and disrupt his plans.
have him build palaces and towers,
to deplete his wealth.
Sixth: send fawning ministers
to make him easily attackable.
Seventh: strengthen his remonstrating ministers,
to make them kill themselves.
Eighth: make your own state rich,
and prepare sharp weapons.
Ninth: sharpen armor and weapons to strike when they are weakened.
All these nine methods—
the king should keep silent and not divulge,
guard them mysteriously.
Then taking the world is not difficult,
let alone Wú?"
King Yuè said:
"Excellent!"
Then he implemented the first method,
establishing the eastern suburb to worship the yang,
named Dōng Huáng Gōng.
Establishing the western suburb to worship the yin,
named Xī Wáng Mǔ.
He sacrificed to the mountain spirits at Kuài Jī,
and honored the water spirits at Jiāng Zhōu.
After serving ghosts and spirits for a year,
the state suffered no disasters.
King Yuè said:
"Splendid!
The methods of the great minister."
I wish to discuss the rest."
Zhǒng said:
"The King of Wú is fond of building palaces,
and never ceases their construction.
The king selects famous mountains and divine timber,
which I respectfully offer to him."
The King of Yuè then sent over three thousand woodworkers,
into the mountains to cut trees.
After a year,
the laborers had achieved nothing.
The workers longed to return home,
all harboring resentment,
and sang the Woodcutter's Chant.
One night,
a pair of divine trees grew naturally,
twenty arm-spans in girth,
fifty fathoms in length,
the male being patterned catalpa,
the female being pián and nán wood.
Skilled craftsmen applied frames,
shaping them with compass and line,
carving and smoothing them round,
engraving, cutting, and polishing,
dividing them with cinnabar and azurite,
inlaying patterned designs,
adorning them with white jade discs,
engraving with gold,
their forms resembling dragons and snakes,
their patterns radiant with light.
Then he sent Grand Master Zhǒng to present them to the King of Wú.
He said:
"The labor-subject from the Eastern Sea, the solitary servant Gōu Jiàn, has sent me, Zhǒng,
daring to through your humble officer,
inform Your Majesty:
Relying on the Great King's power,
I have presumptuously built a small hall,
and have leftover timber,
which I reverently offer with repeated bows to the Great King."
The King of Wú was greatly pleased.
Zǐxū admonished:
"Do not accept it, King.
In the past, Jié built the Líng Terrace,
Zhòu built the Lù Terrace,
yīn and yáng were not in harmony,
cold and heat came untimely,
the five grains did not ripen,
Heaven sent them disasters,
the people were destitute and the state transformed,
leading to their destruction.
If you accept this, Great King,
you will certainly be slain by the King of Yuè."
The King of Wú did not listen,
and accepted them to build the Gūsū Tower.
Three years were spent gathering materials,
five years until completion,
so high it could be seen from two hundred lǐ away.
Travelers on the road,
died on the path and wept in the alleys,
the sounds of sighs and laments unceasing,
the people exhausted, the scholars suffering,
no one had means to live.
The King of Yuè said:
"Excellent!
This is the second strategy."
In the eleventh year,
the King of Yuè pondered deeply and thought long,
desiring only to attack Wú,
and requested Jì Kuǎ for counsel, asking:
"I wish to attack Wú,
but fear I cannot defeat them.
I plan to raise an army early,
and seek your advice."
Jì Kuǎ replied:
"To raise an army and launch troops,
one must first store grain within,
fill with gold and silver,
replenish the treasuries,
and sharpen the weapons.
For all these four,
one must observe the energies of heaven and earth,
trace the origins of yīn and yáng,
understand the solitary and empty,
examine survival and perish,
then one can measure the enemy."
The King of Yuè said:
"Heaven and earth's survival and perish,
what is their essence?"
Jì Kuǎ said:
"The energies of heaven and earth,
determine things' death and life.
Tracing yīn and yáng,
reveals things' nobility and baseness;
understanding the solitary and empty,
knows opportunities and encounters;
examining survival and perish,
distinguishes truth and falsehood."
The King of Yuè said:
"What are death and life, truth and falsehood?"
Jì Kuǎ said:
"In spring, plant the eight grains,
in summer, they grow and nurture,
in autumn, mature and gather,
in winter, store and preserve.
If the season offers growth but one fails to plant,
that is the first death.
Summer growth without seedlings,
second death.
Autumn maturity without gathering,
third death.
Winter storage without reserves,
fourth death.
Even with the virtue of Yáo and Shùn,
there is nothing to be done.
When the season offers growth,
the elders encourage,
the workers are few,
responding to the natural cycles and numbers,
not losing their principles,
that is the first life.
Pay attention and inspect carefully,
diligently remove weeds,
with weeds gone, seedlings flourish,
second life.
Prepare equipment in advance,
harvest when crops are ready,
the state has no tax arrears,
the people lose no ears of grain,
third life.
Granaries sealed and plastered,
old grain removed, new brought in,
the ruler joyful, ministers happy,
men and women trustworthy,
fourth life.
As for yīn and yáng,
in the years ruled by Tàiyīn,
it lingers for three years,
and nobility and baseness become apparent.
The solitary and empty,
refer to the Gate of Heaven and Door of Earth.
Survival and perish,
lie in the ruler's virtue and moral character."
The King of Yuè said:
"How is it that you are so young, yet understand the growth of things?"
Jì Kuǎ said:
"A person of fine qualities,
is not constrained by age."
The King of Yuè said:
"Excellent!
Your way is profound."
Then he looked up to observe celestial patterns,
gathered and examined the constellations,
calculated the movements of the four seasons,
using the lower to infer the upper,
established eight granaries in theory,
storing according to yīn,
selling out when expecting yáng,
devising the ultimate plan,
in three years, wealth increased fivefold,
and Yuè became prosperous and rich.
Gōu Jiàn sighed and said:
"I shall achieve hegemony.
Excellent!
Thanks to Jì Kuǎ's strategies."
In the twelfth year,
King Yuè said to Minister Zhǒng:
"I have heard that the King of Wú is licentious and fond of women,
deluded and sunk in dissipation,
paying no heed to governmental affairs.
If we exploit this to plot against him,
would it be feasible?"
Zhǒng replied:
"He can be overthrown.
Since the King of Wú is licentious and fond of women,
and his minister Pǐ is cunning and caters to his desires,
if we send him beautiful women,
he will certainly accept them.
I beg Your Majesty to select two beautiful women and present them."
The King of Yuè said:
"Excellent."
He then sent a physiognomist throughout the country,
who found two girls gathering firewood on Zhùluó Mountain named Xī Shī and Zhèng Dàn.
They were adorned in fine silks,
taught elegant postures and gait,
trained in an earthen-walled town,
practiced in the capital's lanes,
and after three years of training, they were presented to Wú.
He then had Chancellor Fàn Lí present them, saying:
"King Gōu Jiàn of Yuè humbly has two orphaned girls.
Yuè is low-lying and impoverished,
daring not to detain them,
so he respectfully sends me, Lí, to offer them to Your Majesty.
Despite their plain and unadorned appearance,
we hope you will accept them for menial tasks."
The King of Wú was greatly pleased,
saying:
"Yuè's tribute of two women
is proof of Gōu Jiàn's utmost loyalty to Wú."
Wǔ Zǐxū admonished:
"It must not be;
do not accept them, Your Majesty.
I have heard that the five colors can blind one's eyes,
and the five sounds can deafen one's ears.
In the past, Jié underestimated Tāng and perished,
and Zhòu underestimated King Wén and fell.
If Your Majesty accepts them,
calamity will surely follow.
I have heard that the King of Yuè studies documents tirelessly from dawn,
recites through the night,
and has gathered tens of thousands of daring warriors;
if this man lives,
he will surely achieve his ambition.
The King of Yuè practices sincerity and benevolence,
heeds advice, and promotes the worthy;
if this man lives,
he will surely attain renown.
The King of Yuè wears fur in summer
and thin cloth in winter;
if this man lives,
he will surely become a threat.
I have heard:
Worthy scholars are
the treasure of a state;
beautiful women are
its curse.
Xià perished because of Mò Xǐ,
Yīn fell because of Dá Jǐ,
and Zhōu was lost because of Bāo Sì."
The King of Wú did not listen
and accepted the women.
The King of Yuè said:
"Splendid!
This is the third stratagem."
In the thirteenth year,
King of Yuè said to Minister Wén Zhǒng:
"I have benefited from your strategies,
the plans have all been auspicious,
never failing to succeed.
Now I wish to plot against Wú again,
what should be done?"
Zhǒng replied:
"Your Majesty should proclaim that Yuè is a humble state,
with poor harvests of grain,
and request to purchase grain to satisfy their intentions.
If Heaven wishes to abandon Wú,
they will surely grant Your Majesty's request."
Yuè then sent Minister Wén Zhǒng as envoy to Wú,
seeking audience with the King of Wú through Chief Steward Pǐ,
stating:
"Yuè is a low-lying land,
where floods and droughts are irregular,
grain harvests are poor,
the people suffer from hunger and poverty,
and famine repeatedly strikes the roads.
We wish to request to purchase grain from Great King,
and will repay the state granary next year.
We beg Great King to save us from our destitution."
The King of Wú said:
"The King of Yuè is faithful, sincere, and upholds the Way,
harboring no duplicity.
Now in poverty he comes to plead,
how could I begrudge my wealth and treasures,
and deny his wish?"
Wǔ Zǐxū admonished:
"This must not be!
If Wú does not possess Yuè,
then Yuè will surely possess Wú.
Auspiciousness departs as misfortune arrives -
this is to nourish a living enemy and destroy one's own state!
Giving them grain does not make them kin,
not giving does not create enmity.
Moreover, Yuè has a sagacious minister Fàn Lǐ,
courageous and skilled in strategy,
who will prepare for attack and warfare,
awaiting our moment of weakness.
Observing that the King of Yuè sent an envoy to request grain,
it is not because the state is poor and people are suffering that they ask for grain,
but to enter our state,
and watch for our king's moment of inattention."
The King of Wú said:
"I have humbled the King of Yuè,
and taken possession of his people,
caring for his altars of soil and grain,
making Gōu Jiàn feel ashamed.
Gōu Jiàn is submissive in spirit,
driving my carriage,
walking backward before my horse -
all the feudal lords have heard of this.
Now that I have allowed him to return to his country,
to serve his ancestral temple,
and restore his altars of soil and grain,
how would he dare to harbor thoughts of rebelling against me?"
Wǔ Zǐxū said:
"I have heard that when a gentleman is in distress, it is not difficult for him to suppress his heart and humble himself before others,
but later he will show expressions that provoke others.
I have heard that the King of Yuè is hungry,
and his people are in dire straits -
this is an opportunity to destroy them.
Now if we do not follow the way of Heaven,
and comply with the principles of Earth,
but instead supply them with food,
following the ruler's command,
it is like the fox and pheasant sporting together.
The fox lowers its body,
and the pheasant trusts it.
Thus the fox achieves its aim,
and the pheasant must die.
Should we not be cautious?"
The King of Wú said:
"Gōu Jiàn's state faces difficulties,
and I provide them with grain.
Kindness goes forth and righteousness returns,
this virtue is shining bright -
what is there to worry about?"
Wǔ Zǐxū said:
"I have heard that wolf cubs have wild hearts,
and enemies should not be treated with intimacy.
A tiger should not be fed,
and a venomous snake should not be allowed to follow its will.
Now Great King donates the state's blessings,
to enrich a useless enemy,
rejects the words of loyal ministers,
and complies with the desires of foes.
I will surely see Yuè destroy Wú,
with wild deer roaming the Gūxū Terrace,
and thorns overrunning the palace gates.
I hope Your Majesty will consider King Wǔ's campaign against King Zhòu."
Chief Steward Pǐ responded from the side:
"King Wǔ was not a minister of King Zhòu,
yet he led feudal lords to attack his ruler -
although he defeated Yīn, can this be called righteous?"
Wǔ Zǐxū said:
"King Wǔ thereby achieved his fame."
Chief Steward Pǐ said:
"To personally kill one's ruler for fame -
I cannot bear such a thing."
Wǔ Zǐxū said:
"Those who steal states become marquises,
while those who steal gold are executed.
If King Wǔ had lost his principles,
then why would Zhōu be held up as an example for the three dynasties?"
Chief Steward Pǐ said:
"Wǔ Zǐxū as a minister,
merely wishes to interfere with the ruler's preferences,
contradict the ruler's heart,
to show off his own fullness.
Why does the ruler not recognize his faults?"
Wǔ Zǐxū said:
"Chief Steward Pǐ firmly seeks to gain intimacy,
previously releasing the prisoner from the stone chamber,
accepting his gifts of precious women,
forming external relations with enemy states,
and internally confusing the ruler.
Great King should investigate this,
and not be deceived by petty men.
Now Great King is like bathing an infant -
though it cries, do not listen to Chief Steward Pǐ's words."
The King of Wú said:
"Chief Steward Pǐ is correct.
You, sir, upon hearing my words,
do not follow the way of a loyal minister,
but resemble a flattering sycophant."
Chief Steward Pǐ said:
"I have heard that when a neighboring state faces emergency,
rushing to rescue from a thousand miles away -
this is the way of a true king.
Enfeoffing the descendants of destroyed states,
this is how the Five Hegemons supported those facing extinction."
The King of Wú then gave Yuè ten thousand shi of grain,
and commanded them:
"I have gone against my ministers' counsel to supply Yuè,
when the harvest is abundant, return it to me."
Minister Wén Zhǒng said:
"I receive this mission to return to Yuè,
when the year brings good harvest, I will truly repay Wú's loan."
Minister Wén Zhǒng returned to Yuè,
all the ministers of Yuè shouted 'long live',
and immediately distributed the grain as rewards to the ministers,
extending to all the common people.
After two years,
the King of Yuè had ripe grain,
selected the finest grains and steamed them,
then returned them to Wú,
repaying the exact measure in bushels,
again sending Minister Wén Zhǒng to return them to the King of Wú.
The King received Yuè's grain,
heaved a long sigh,
and said to Chief Steward Pǐ:
"The land of Yuè is fertile,
their seeds are excellent,
we should keep them for our people to plant."
Thus Wú planted Yuè's grain,
but the grain seeds were dead and none sprouted,
causing great famine among the people of Wú.
The King of Yuè said:
"They are in dire straits,
we can attack them."
Minister Wén Zhǒng said:
"Not yet.
The state is just beginning to know poverty,
loyal ministers still remain,
Heaven's signs have not appeared,
we must wait for the right time."
The King of Yuè also asked Chancellor Fàn Lǐ:
"I have plans for revenge,
for naval battles we use boats,
for land campaigns we use chariots,
the advantages of chariots and boats,
are inferior to weapons and crossbows.
Now when you plan affairs for me,
is there anything inappropriate?"
Fàn Lǐ replied:
"I have heard that all sage rulers of antiquity practiced warfare and employed soldiers,
but matters of battle formations, troop arrays, and military drums,
the determination of auspicious and inauspicious outcomes lies in their execution.
I have heard that in Yuè there is a maiden,
who comes from the southern forests,
praised by the people of the state.
I hope Your Majesty will invite her,
she can appear immediately."
The King of Yuè then sent an envoy to invite her,
inquiring about the techniques of sword and halberd.
The maiden was going north to see the king,
when on the road she met an old man,
who called himself Lord Yuán.
He asked the maiden:
"I have heard you are skilled with the sword,
I wish to see this."
The maiden said:
"I dare not conceal anything,
please test me, sir."
Thereupon,
Lord Yuán then tapped a Línyū bamboo with his staff,
and the bamboo tip snapped off from the treetop but did not fall to the ground.
The woman swiftly caught its end,
while Lord Yuán flew up into a tree,
transforming into a white ape.
He then bid farewell and left,
and she went to see the King of Yuè.
The King of Yuè asked:
"What is the way of the sword like?"
The woman replied:
"I was born in the depths of the forest,
raised in the wilderness where no one dwells,
and there is no art I have not practiced.
I do not associate with feudal lords,
but privately I love the art of striking,
reciting it ceaselessly.
I did not receive it from anyone else,
yet suddenly it became my own."
The King of Yuè said:
"How is this art?"
The woman said:
"The art is very subtle and easy,
its meaning very obscure and profound.
The way has its gates and doors,
and also its yīn and yáng;
opening the gate and closing the door,
yīn declines and yáng rises.
In all methods of hand combat,
internally, one should be rich in spirit,
externally, display a calm demeanor.
Appearing like a gentle woman,
but striking like a startled tiger.
Arrange the form and await the energy,
moving together with the spirit.
Vague as the sun,
fleeting as a darting rabbit.
Chasing forms and pursuing shadows,
the light seems to flicker.
Breathing in and out,
unconstrained by rules or restrictions.
Horizontal, vertical, adverse, or favorable,
straight or bent, unheard of.
This art
enables one to stand against a hundred,
a hundred to stand against ten thousand.
If Your Majesty wishes to test it,
the proof will be immediately evident."
The King of Yuè then bestowed a title upon the woman,
naming her:
"The Maiden of Yuè."
He then ordered the captains of the five companies to learn and teach her techniques to the soldiers.
At that time, none could surpass the sword of the Maiden of Yuè.
Thereupon, Fàn Lǐ recommended another expert archer, Chén Yīn.
Chén Yīn
was a man of Chǔ.
The King of Yuè invited Chén Yīn and asked him:
"I have heard that you are skilled in archery;
from where does this art originate?"
Chén Yīn said:
"Your servant
is a humble man from Chǔ,
who has practiced archery,
but does not fully understand its principles."
The King of Yuè said:
"Very well,
I wish you to explain it in detail."
Chén Yīn said:
"Your servant has heard that the crossbow originated from the bow,
the bow from the slingshot,
and the slingshot began with an ancient filial son."
The King of Yuè said:
"What about this filial son and the slingshot?"
Chén Yīn said:
"In ancient times,
people were simple and unadorned,
eating birds and beasts when hungry,
drinking mist and dew when thirsty.
When they died, they were wrapped in white reeds
and left in the wilderness.
A filial son could not bear to see his parents eaten by birds and beasts,
so he made a slingshot to guard them,
preventing harm from birds and beasts.
Hence, a song says:
'Cut bamboo, join bamboo,
fling earth, chase away harm'—that is what it means.
Then, Shénnóng Huángdì strung wood to make a bow,
and sharpened wood to make arrows.
The effectiveness of bow and arrow
awed the four directions.
After Huángdì,
in Chǔ there was Hùfù.
Hùfù
was born in the Jīng Mountains of Chǔ,
and never saw his parents in his life.
As a child,
he practiced using bow and arrow,
and never missed his shot.
He passed his art on to Yì,
Yì passed it to Péng Méng,
and Péng Méng passed it to Qín Shì of Chǔ.
Qín Shì believed that bow and arrow were not sufficient to awe the world.
At that time,
feudal lords attacked each other,
and weapons clashed everywhere.
The power of bow and arrow could not subdue them.
Qín Shì then set the bow horizontally on the arm,
added a trigger and mechanism,
and applied force to it,
after which the feudal lords could be subdued.
Qín Shì passed it on to the three lords of Chǔ,
namely, Gōudǎn, È, and Zhāng,
who were titled Mí Hóu, Yì Hóu, and Wèi Hóu.
From the three lords of Chǔ, it was passed down to King Ling,
and through generations in Chǔ,
they used peach-wood bows and thorn-wood arrows to defend against neighboring states.
After King Ling,
the art of archery branched into different schools,
with various experts applying it,
but none grasped its true essence.
Your servant's predecessors received it in Chǔ,
and it has been five generations down to me.
Though I do not fully understand the art,
I ask Your Majesty to test it."
The King of Yuè said:
"What principles govern the form of the crossbow?"
Chén Yīn said:
"The frame is like a walled city,
guarding the subjects.
The stock is like the ruler,
from whom commands originate.
The trigger is like the law enforcer,
controlling the officers.
The nut is like the central general,
managing the inner core.
The latch is like the defender,
checking advance and retreat.
The stirrup is like the attendant,
heeding the ruler's orders.
The stock is like the road,
conveying the commands.
The bow is like the general,
bearing the heavy load.
The string is like the strategist,
directing the warriors.
The bolt is like the flying envoy,
carrying out the mission.
The metal tip is like the true enemy,
advancing unceasingly.
The fletching is like the deputy envoy,
guiding the true path.
The nock is like the receiver of orders,
knowing what is feasible.
The binding is like the commandant,
securing left and right.
The target is like the hundred deaths,
not to be feared.
Birds have no time to fly,
beasts no chance to flee.
Where the crossbow is aimed,
none escape death.
In my humble opinion,
the principles are all thus."
The King of Yuè said:
"I wish to hear about the proper way of shooting."
Chén Yīn said:
"I have heard that the proper way of shooting
is comprehensive yet subtle.
The sages of old
could name their target before the crossbow was fired.
I cannot match the sages of old,
but let me explain the essentials:
In the art of shooting,
the body should be as if supporting a plank,
the head as if balancing an egg.
The left foot steps, the right foot is set firm,
the left hand as if clinging to a branch,
the right hand as if holding a child.
Raise the crossbow, eye the enemy,
hold the breath, calm the mind.
Release with the exhalation,
achieving harmony.
With spirit settled and thoughts focused,
movement and stillness are distinct.
The right hand releases the trigger,
the left hand remains unaware.
One body follows different teachings,
how much more so the distinction between male and female.
This is the proper way of holding and shooting the crossbow."
"I wish to hear about the method of observing the enemy's posture and releasing the flying bolt with precision."
Chén Yīn said:
"In the art of shooting,
align the sight with the enemy,
combining with a triple connection.
The crossbow has its draw weight,
the bolts their lightness or heaviness.
For each stone of draw weight, take one liang,
then the numbers will balance.
For distance, high or low,
seek accuracy down to the zhū and fēn.
The essence of the art lies herein."
There were no last words."
The King of Yuè said:
"Excellent.
Exhaust your way,
I wish you to teach it entirely to the people of my state."
Yīn said:
"The Way comes from Heaven,
matters lie with humans.
What humans practice,
there is nothing that cannot become divine."
Thereupon,
he had Chén Yīn teach the soldiers to practice archery outside the northern suburbs.
After three months,
the soldiers were all able to master the skill of bows and crossbows.
When Chén Yīn died,
the King of Yuè mourned him,
buried him in the west of the state,
and named his burial place "Chén Yīn Shān."
In the fifteenth year of Gōu Jiàn's reign,
he planned to attack Wú
and said to Minister Wén Zhǒng:
"I employed your strategies
to escape the punishment of heaven's scourge
and return to my state.
I have truly spoken to the people of our state,
and they are pleased.
Yet you once said:
'When there are heavenly signs, come and present them.'
Now, is there any response?"
Zhǒng replied:
"The reason Wú is strong
is because of Wǔ Zǐxū.
Now that Wǔ Zǐxū has died due to his loyal remonstrations,
this is a heavenly sign foretelling their state's destruction.
I hope you will devote your heart and mind to speaking with the people."
King Yuè said:
"Hear what I told our people:
'I did not know my strength was insufficient,
and sought revenge against a great state,
exposing our people's bones on the central plains -
this is my crime.
I shall truly change my methods.'
Thereupon,
we buried the dead and inquired after the wounded,
condoled with the grieving,
congratulated the joyful,
bade farewell to those leaving and welcomed those arriving,
and removed what harmed the people.
Then I humbly served Fū Chāi,
sending three hundred officials to Wú.
Wú granted me a territory of several hundred lǐ,
whereupon I made a covenant with the elders and brothers of Wú, swearing:
'I have heard that in ancient times, when there was a worthy ruler,
the people from all directions would flock to him like water.
Now that I cannot govern properly,
I shall lead you, my men and their wives, to serve as protective screens.'
I ordered that young men should not marry old women,
nor old men marry young women.
If a girl reached seventeen without marrying,
her parents would be held guilty.
If a man reached twenty without taking a wife,
his parents would be held guilty.
Those about to give birth were to report to me,
and I would have physicians attend them.
For giving birth to two boys,
they were rewarded with a pot of wine and a dog.
For giving birth to two girls,
they were given a pot of wine and a pig.
For bearing three children,
I provided a wet nurse.
For bearing two children,
I provided a caretaker.
If the eldest son died,
I suspended my governance for three years;
if the youngest son died,
I suspended it for three months.
I would mourn and bury them as if they were my own children.
I ordered that orphans, widows, the ill, and the impoverished
should have their children taken in by the government.
Those wishing to serve
were provided housing according to their status,
fine clothes,
ample food,
and selected for their sharpness.
All scholars coming from the four directions
were received at court with courtesy.
I carried food and soup while traveling through the state.
When children playing in the state encountered me,
I would feed them,
showing affection,
and ask their names.
They would not eat unless it was food from me,
nor wear clothes unless provided by my wife.
For seven years, I collected no taxes from the state,
yet the people had three years' worth of stores at home.
Men sang with joy,
women gathered and laughed.
Now the elders of our state daily petition me, saying:
'Formerly, Fū Chāi humiliated our king before the feudal lords,
bringing lasting shame upon us in the world.
Now Yuè is wealthy and prosperous,
and our king is frugal.
We request permission to avenge this disgrace.'
I declined, saying:
'In the past, when I was humiliated,
it was not your fault,
but my own.
How dare someone like me
trouble the people of our state
to settle my old grudges?'
The elders petitioned again:
'Throughout Yuè's four borders,
we are all your subjects.
A son avenges his father,
a minister repays his lord's grievances -
how could anyone not exert their full effort?
We beg to fight again,
to eliminate our king's longstanding enemies.'
I happily agreed."
Minister Wén Zhǒng said:
"I observe that the King of Wú, having achieved his ambitions against Qí and Jìn,
should have proceeded to cross into our territory
with troops approaching our borders.
Yet now his army is weary and resting,
for a year without testing us,
as if forgetting about us.
We cannot be lax.
I shall divine the heavens.
The people of Wú are already exhausted from military service,
worn out by fighting,
markets lack even red rice stores,
state granaries are empty,
the people must have thoughts of moving away,
seeking cold clams and snails along the eastern seashore.
Observing human affairs through omens
is also revealed through divination.
If you raise an army now
to exploit advantageous opportunities,
and attack Wú's border regions,
it would be inadvisable to proceed.
Even if the King of Wú has no intention of attacking us,
and even if we provoke his anger,
it would be better to wait for the right moment
to understand his intentions."
King Yuè said:
"I have no desire for campaigns,
but the people have been requesting war for three years now,
and I cannot but follow the people's wishes.
Now I hear Wén Zhǒng's difficult advice."
The elders of Yuè again advised:
"Wú can be attacked.
If we win, we destroy their state;
if not, we still wear down their troops.
If Wú survives,
you can make a covenant with them,
and your achievements will be known among the feudal lords."
The king said:
"Good."
Thereupon,
he assembled all his ministers and commanded them:
"Whoever dares to advise against attacking Wú
will not be pardoned."
Fàn Lǐ and Wén Zhǒng said to each other:
"Our advice has already been rejected,
yet we must still obey the king's command."
King Yuè assembled the army, arrayed the officers, and greatly exhorted the multitude,
swearing to them:
"I have heard that the worthy rulers of old
did not worry about having insufficient numbers,
but feared their people lacked shame in ambition and conduct.
Now Fū Chāi has one hundred thirty thousand troops armored in rhinoceros hide,
yet he doesn't worry about their lack of shame in ambition and conduct,
but fears his numbers are insufficient.
Now I shall assist heaven's might.
I do not want the minor courage of reckless men;
I want soldiers who think of rewards when advancing,
and avoid punishment when retreating."
Thereupon, the people of Yuè - fathers encouraging sons,
elder brothers urging younger brothers -
said:
"Wú can be attacked."
King Yuè again summoned Fàn Lǐ and asked:
"Wú has already killed Zǐxū,
and flatterers abound.
Our people again urge me to attack Wú -
can we attack?"
Fàn Lǐ said:
"Not yet.
We must wait until next spring, then it will be possible."
The king asked:
"Why?"
Fàn Lǐ said:
"I observe the King of Wú is meeting with feudal lords north at Huángchí,
taking his elite troops with him,
leaving the state empty,
with only the old and weak remaining behind,
and the crown prince guarding the capital.
His troops have just left the border, not far yet;
if they hear Yuè is attacking their undefended territory,
they can easily return.
Better to wait until coming spring."
That summer, on the bingzǐ day of the sixth month,
Gōu Jiàn asked again,
and Fàn Lǐ said:
"Now we can attack."
Then he dispatched two thousand trained marines, forty thousand elite soldiers, six thousand gentlemen, and one thousand various officers,
engaging Wú in battle on the yǐyǒu day.
On the bingxū day, they captured and killed the crown prince.
On the dīnghài day, they entered Wú,
burning the Gūxū Tower.
Wú sent urgent word to Fū Chāi,
who was then meeting with feudal lords at Huángchí.
Fearing the world would hear of it,
he immediately sealed the news, not allowing leaks.
After concluding the covenant at Huángchí,
he sent someone to seek peace with Yuè.
Gōu Jiàn, considering himself unable to annihilate them yet,
Thereupon, they made peace with Wú.
In the twenty-first year,
in the seventh month,
the King of Yuè again mobilized all the troops in the country to attack Wú.
It happened that the Chǔ envoy Shēn Bāoxū was on a diplomatic mission in Yuè,
so the King of Yuè asked Bāoxū:
"Is Wú attackable?"
Shēn Bāoxū replied:
"Your subject is unskilled in strategy,
and insufficient for divination."
The King of Yuè said:
"Wú has acted unjustly,
destroyed our altars of land and grain,
razed our ancestral temples,
turning them into plains,
preventing us from making blood sacrifices.
I wish to contend with them for Heaven's favor,
and though my chariots, horses, weapons, armor, and troops are all prepared,
I lack the means to employ them.
I sincerely inquire about warfare,
what makes it feasible?"
Shēn Bāoxū said:
"Your subject is ignorant and cannot know."
The King of Yuè pressed him further,
and Bāoxū then said:
"Now Wú
is a strong state,
able to gain broadly from the various lords.
May I ask what basis Your Majesty has for fighting them?"
The King of Yuè said:
"Those by my side,
when they drink and eat meat,
I have never failed to share with them.
My own food and drink lack fine flavors,
my music listening lacks full enjoyment,
all seeking to repay Wú.
I wish to fight with this."
Bāoxū said:
"Good though it is,
it is not sufficient for war."
The King of Yuè said:
"Throughout Yuè,
I broadly love and treat them as my children,
loyally and kindly nurturing them.
I have cultivated good laws and lenient punishments,
desiring what the people desire,
eliminating what the people hate,
praising their goodness,
covering their faults,
seeking to repay Wú.
I wish to fight with this."
Bāoxū said:
"Good though it is,
it is not sufficient for war."
The King said:
"Throughout Yuè,
I comfort the wealthy,
I provide for the poor,
relieving their shortages,
reducing their surplus,
ensuring that poor and rich do not lose their benefits,
seeking to repay Wú.
I wish to fight with this."
Bāoxū said:
"Good though it is,
it is not sufficient for war."
The King said:
