"Our state borders Chǔ to the south,
approaches Jìn to the west,
faces Qí to the north,
in spring and autumn presenting coins, jades, silks, sons and daughters as tribute,
never daring to cease,
seeking to repay Wú.
I wish to fight with this."
Bāoxū said:
"Excellent!
Nothing could surpass this,
yet war is still not feasible.
The way of warfare
begins with wisdom,
follows with benevolence,
and is decided with courage.
If the ruler lacks wisdom,
then he has no adaptable strategies,
to distinguish the numbers of many and few.
Without benevolence,
then he cannot share the hardships of hunger and cold with the three armies,
nor align with their joys and sufferings.
Without courage,
then he cannot resolve doubts about advance and retreat,
nor decide debates on feasibility."
Thereupon,
the King of Yuè said:
"I respectfully obey your command."
In the tenth month of winter,
the King of Yuè then consulted the eight great officers saying:
"Formerly Wú acted unjustly,
destroyed our ancestral temples,
razed our altars of land and grain,
turning them into plains,
preventing blood sacrifices.
I wish to contend with them for Heaven's favor,
though weapons and armor are prepared,
I lack the means to employ them.
I inquired of Shēn Bāoxū,
and he has already instructed me.
I dare to ask you great officers,
what should be done?"
Great officer Yè Yōng said:
"With careful rewards, war is feasible.
Be careful in rewards,
clear in trustworthiness,
none without merit shall receive,
those with merit must be rewarded,
then officers and soldiers will not be negligent."
The King said:
"Sagely!"
Great officer Kǔchéng said:
"With careful punishments, war is feasible.
Careful punishments make officers and soldiers fearful upon sight,
not daring to disobey orders."
The King said:
"Courageous!"
Great officer Wén Zhǒng said:
"With careful assessment of things, war is feasible.
Careful assessment distinguishes right from wrong,
clear discernment of right and wrong,
leaves none able to deceive."
The King said:
"Discerning!"
Great officer Fàn Lǐ said:
"With careful preparation, war is feasible.
Careful preparation includes defense,
awaiting the unexpected,
preparations established and defenses solid,
certainly able to respond to difficulties."
The King said:
"Prudent!"
Great officer Gāo Rú said:
"With careful attention to reputation, war is feasible.
Be careful regarding reputation,
to distinguish purity from corruption.
Purity and corruption
refer to our ruler's fame,
heard in the Zhōu court,
making the various lords not resentful externally."
The King said:
"Appropriate!"
Great officer Fú Tóng said:
"With broad kindness and knowing one's lot, war is feasible.
Broad kindness through extensive giving,
knowing one's lot without overstepping."
The King said:
"Divine!"
Great officer Jì Niè said:
"Observe heaven and examine earth,
correlate and respond to changes,
then war is feasible.
Heavenly changes, earthly responses, and human ways favorable,
these three appearing in advance,
then it is feasible."
The King said:
"Enlightened!"
Thereupon,
Gōu Jiàn withdrew to fast and commanded the people saying:
"I will have unexpected plans,
from near to far,
none shall fail to hear."
Then he again ordered the officials and the people saying:
"Those who obey commands will be rewarded,
all must arrive at the state gate by the appointed time,
those who disobey commands,
I will publicly execute."
Gōu Jiàn feared the people would not trust him,
so he made known his campaign against injustice,
heard in the Zhōu court,
making the various lords not resentful externally,
and commanded within the state:
"Within five days,
you shall be my good people.
After five days,
you are not my people,
and will furthermore be punished with execution."
When the commands were implemented,
he went to give orders to his wife.
The King stood with his back to the screen,
his wife faced the screen standing,
The King said:
"From this day onward,
internal affairs shall not go out,
external affairs shall not come in.
Each shall keep to their duties,
to fulfill their trust.
If there is disgrace within the inner chambers,
that is your responsibility.
If there is disgrace a thousand lǐ beyond our borders,
that is my responsibility.
I meet with you here,
to make this clear warning."
The King left the palace.
The lady saw the king off only as far as the screen.
The king then turned back and closed the door,
sealing it with earth.
The lady removed her hairpin,
sat on a mat set aside,
calmed her heart without adornment,
and did not sweep for three months.
When the king went out, she again stood with her back to the wall,
and the ministers faced the wall with respect.
The king then commanded his ministers, saying:
"If the distribution of land is unequal,
and the soil is not well cultivated,
causing me disgrace in the state,
it is your fault.
Facing the enemy without fighting,
and the soldiers not being willing to die,
bringing shame upon the lords,
and ruining achievements under heaven,
it is my responsibility.
From now on,
internal affairs shall not go out,
and external affairs shall not come in.
I have firmly admonished you."
The ministers respectfully accepted the command,
and the king then went out.
The ministers saw him off beyond the wall,
closed the gate of the outer palace,
and sealed it with earth.
The ministers sat on mats set aside,
refrained from the five flavors,
and did not respond to persuasions.
Gōu Jiàn gave orders to the lady and the ministers, saying:
"The state has its defenses."
He then sat on an open altar,
arranged drums and had them beaten,
the army formed into battle arrays,
and immediately executed three guilty men,
parading them before the army,
commanding:
"Those who do not follow my orders will end up like this."
The next day,
he moved the army to the outskirts,
executed three guilty men,
paraded them before the army,
and commanded:
"Those who do not follow my orders will end up like this."
The king then ordered those in the state who would not march,
bidding them farewell and telling them:
"You stay peacefully on your land and fulfill your duties,
while I go to campaign against the enemy of our ancestral temple,
to make amends to you all."
He ordered the people each to send their sons and brothers to the border outskirts.
The soldiers each bid farewell to their fathers, brothers, and kin.
The people were sorrowful,
all composing words of parting and departure,
saying:
"Leaping fiercely, crushing the long evil,
wielding halberds, driving spears.
Where we part, none shall surrender,
to vent our king's vital breath.
The three armies soar down at once,
all they face shall perish.
One warrior resolved to die,
matches a hundred men.
The Way blesses the virtuous,
the Wú troops will slaughter themselves.
Avenge our king's long-standing shame,
awe shaking the eight capitals.
The ranks are hard to change,
mighty as pí chū beasts.
March on, each striving hard,
alas, alas!"
Thereupon,
none among the onlookers was not heartbroken.
The next day,
he moved the army again to the border,
executed three guilty men,
paraded them before the army,
saying:
"Those who disobey orders will be like this."
Three days later,
he moved the army again to Zuìlǐ,
executed three guilty men,
paraded them before the army,
saying:
"Those with wicked hearts, hidden deeds, unfit to face the enemy will be like this."
Gōu Jiàn then ordered the officials to widely proclaim to the army,
saying:
"Those who have parents but no brothers,
come and report to me.
I have great matters at hand,
you leave your parents' care, the love of your elders,
to answer the state's urgency.
If you are in the midst of army conflicts,
and your parents or brothers fall ill,
I will regard their illness as that of my own parents and brothers.
If any die,
I will bury and send them off,
as I would for my own parents and brothers who die and are buried."
The next day,
he proclaimed again to the army,
saying:
"Soldiers who are ill,
unable to follow the army and join the troops,
I will provide them with doctors and medicine,
supply them with gruel,
and eat the same as they do."
The next day,
he proclaimed again to the army,
saying:
"Those whose strength is insufficient to bear armor and weapons,
whose will and conduct are inadequate to heed the king's command,
I will lighten their heavy loads,
and harmonize their duties."
The next day,
he rotated the army to the south of the river,
revised the strict battle formations,
and executed five more guilty men,
proclaiming:
"I cherish my soldiers,
even my own son cannot surpass this.
But when they incur execution,
even my own son cannot escape it."
Fearing the soldiers might be too afraid of the laws to be effective,
he thought he had not yet gained their utmost loyalty in death.
On the way, he saw a frog puffing its belly in anger,
displaying a warlike spirit,
and he saluted it by touching the crossbar of his chariot.
One of his soldiers asked the king:
"Why does my lord respect a frog and salute it?"
Gōu Jiàn said:
"I have long desired the anger of my soldiers,
but none have met my expectations.
Now this frog is a creature without knowledge,
yet it shows anger upon seeing an enemy,
hence I salute it."
Thereupon,
when the soldiers heard this,
none did not harbor a heart willing to die joyfully,
each pledging his life.
The officials and generals widely proclaimed to the army:
"Each squad command its own unit,
each unit command its own soldiers.
To return and not return,
to stay and not stay,
to advance and not advance,
to retreat and not retreat,
to go left and not left,
to go right and not right,
those who do not follow orders,
will be executed."
Thereupon,
Wú deployed all its troops north of the river,
while Yuè's army was south of the river.
The King of Yuè divided his forces into left and right armies,
all clad in rhinoceros hide armor,
and ordered the men of Ān Guǎng to carry stone-tipped arrows,
and draw Lú Shēng's crossbows,
personally leading the army of gentlemen, six thousand men, as the central formation.
The next day,
about to battle at the river,
he gave orders at dusk to the left army,
to march silently upriver for five lǐ,
and await the Wú troops.
He also ordered the right army,
to cross the river silently for ten lǐ,
and also await the Wú troops.
At midnight,
he had the left and right armies wade across the river beating drums,
waiting in midstream for Wú to advance.
The Wú army heard this,
was greatly alarmed,
and said to each other:
"Now the Yuè army is divided into two forces,
intending to attack us from both sides."
So they also divided their forces in the dark of night,
to surround Yuè.
The King of Yuè secretly sent his left and right armies to engage Wú in a feint,
with the sound of great drums echoing.
He covertly deployed his private troops of six thousand men,
advancing silently without drums to attack Wú,
and the Wú army was greatly defeated.
Yuè's left and right armies then pursued and attacked,
defeating them decisively at Yòu.
They defeated them again at the outskirts,
and again at the ferry.
Thus, three battles and three defeats,
they advanced directly to Wú,
besieging Wú in the western city.
The King of Wú was greatly terrified,
and fled by night.
The King of Yuè pursued the fugitives,
attacked the Wú troops,
entering Jiāngyáng and Sōnglíng.
As they intended to enter Xūmén,
about six or seven lǐ away,
they looked toward the southern city of Wú,
and saw Wǔ Zǐxū's head,
huge as a cart wheel,
eyes like flashing lightning,
With hair and beard bristling in all directions,
he shot across ten lǐ.
The Yuè army was greatly terrified,
and halted their troops to request passage.
That very night at midnight,
a violent storm and torrential rain arose,
with thunderbolts racing and lightning flashing,
flinging stones and whipping up sand,
swift as arrows from bows and crossbows.
The Yuè army was shattered and defeated,
Sōnglíng retreated,
soldiers lay stiff and dead,
the masses scattered and dispersed,
with none able to rescue or stop it.
Fàn Lǐ and Wén Zhǒng then kowtowed and bared their upper bodies,
bowing in apology to Zǐxū,
wishing to beg for passage.
Zǐxū then appeared to Zhǒng and Lǐ in a dream,
saying:
"I know that Yuè is destined to enter Wú,
so I requested my head be placed at the southern gate,
to witness your destruction of Wú.
I only wished to bring Fūchāi to his end.
But now that you are about to enter my state,
my heart cannot bear it,
so I created wind and rain to repel your army.
However, Yuè's campaign against Wú
is ultimately Heaven's will.
How could I stop it?
If Yuè wishes to enter,
change your approach to the eastern gate,
I will open a path for you through the city,
to clear your way."
Thereupon,
the Yuè army the next day changed course to advance from the river,
entering Hǎiyáng at the Dí River with three routes,
then breached the southeastern corner to get through,
and the Yuè army thus surrounded Wú.
After besieging it for a year,
the Wú forces were repeatedly defeated,
and they eventually drove the King of Wú to take refuge on Gūxū Mountain.
Wú sent Wángsūn Luò, who bared his upper body and advanced on his knees,
to seek peace with the King of Yuè,
saying:
"Your solitary servant Fūchāi,
dares to lay bare his innermost thoughts.
In the past, I offended you at Kuàijī,
and Fūchāi did not dare to defy your command,
but was able to make peace with you, my lord, and return.
Now you, my lord, raise an army to punish your solitary servant,
and I will obey your every command.
I hope that you might consider today's Gūxū
as the Kuàijī of former days.
If by the favor of Heaven's balance,
I could be pardoned from the death penalty,
then Wú is willing to remain your servant forever."
Gōu Jiàn could not bear his words,
and was about to grant him peace.
Fàn Lǐ said:
"In the affair at Kuàijī,
Heaven gave Yuè to Wú,
but Wú did not take it.
Now Heaven gives Wú to Yuè,
can Yuè defy this mandate?
Moreover, my lord, you have risen early and retired late,
gnashing your teeth and engraving it in your bones,
planning for over twenty years—
was it not all for this one day's event?
To obtain it today and then abandon it—
can such a plan be right?
When Heaven gives and you do not take,
you will instead suffer the calamity.
How can you, my lord, forget the distress of Kuàijī?"
Gōu Jiàn said:
"I wish to heed your words,
but I cannot bear to face their envoy."
Fàn Lǐ then sounded the drums and advanced the troops,
saying:
"The king has already delegated governance to his officers;
envoy, leave quickly,
lest you incur blame without delay."
The Wú envoy left in tears.
Gōu Jiàn pitied him,
and sent someone to tell the King of Wú:
"I will place you at Yǒngdōng,
providing you and your wife with over three hundred people,
to live out your days as a king—
is that acceptable?"
The King of Wú declined, saying:
"Since Heaven has brought disaster upon Wú,
not before or after,
but precisely upon my person,
causing the loss and destruction of the ancestral temples and altars of state—
the land and people, the ministers of Wú,
Yuè already possesses them.
I am old,
and cannot serve you as king."
He then fell on his sword and committed suicide.
After Gōu Jiàn had destroyed Wú,
he led his troops north across the Jiāng and Huái,
and met with the lords of Qí, Jìn, and other states at Xúzhōu,
presenting tribute to Zhōu.
King Yuán of Zhōu sent someone to bestow gifts upon Gōu Jiàn.
Having received the mandate and title,
he left and returned to Jiāngnán.
He gave the land north of the Huái to Chǔ,
returned the territory Wú had seized from Sòng,
and gave Lǔ a hundred lǐ east of the Sì River.
At that time,
the Yuè army dominated over the Jiāng and Huái,
and the feudal lords all offered congratulations.
The King of Yuè returned to Wú,
and upon returning, asked Fàn Lǐ:
"How did your words so accord with Heaven?"
Fàn Lǐ said:
"This is the way of Sùnǚ;
a single word can align with the affairs of a great king.
When the king asks how it is done,
the essence truly lies in the upper and lower parts of the 'Golden Casket'."
The King of Yuè said:
"Excellent.
If I do not claim the title of king,
can it be fully understood?"
Lǐ said:
"No.
In the past, when Wú claimed kingship,
usurping the title of the Son of Heaven,
Heaven showed changes above,
and the sun was eclipsed.
Now if you, my lord, proceed to usurp the title and do not turn back,
I fear heavenly changes will appear again."
The King of Yuè returned to Wú,
set out a feast at the Wéntái,
and the assembled ministers made merry.
He then ordered music to be played for the song of campaigning against Wú.
The music master said:
"I have heard that one composes tunes for events,
and creates music for achievements.
My king honors virtue,
instructing and transforming states with the Way,
punishing unrighteous men,
avenging wrongs and erasing shame,
imposing awe on the feudal lords,
and receiving the merit of a hegemon and king.
Your merit can be depicted in paintings,
your virtue engraved on metal and stone,
your fame entrusted to strings and pipes,
your name preserved on bamboo and silk.
I beg to take up the qín and play it."
He then performed a piece with clear lyrics, saying:
"Ah, the gathering!
Now we wish to attack Wú—
is it not yet possible?"
Great Masters Zhǒng and Lǐ said:
"Wú killed the loyal minister Wǔ Zǐxū;
if we do not attack Wú now,
what are we waiting for?"
Great Master Zhǒng came forward to propose a toast,
his words being:
"August Heaven aids and blesses,
our king receives good fortune.
Good ministers gather in counsel—
such is our king's virtue.
The ancestral temples assist in governance,
spirits and gods lend their support.
The lord does not forget his ministers,
the ministers exhaust their strength.
The blue, blue sky above
cannot be covered or blocked.
With two shēng of wine in the cup,
may ten thousand blessings be without end."
Thereupon,
the King of Yuè remained silent and said nothing.
Great Master Zhǒng said:
"Our king is wise and benevolent,
embracing the Way and upholding virtue.
He destroyed his enemy and crushed Wú,
yet does not forget to return to his state.
He is unstinting in rewards,
and all evils are blocked.
Ruler and ministers are in harmony,
blessings and protection reach a thousand million.
With two shēng of wine in the cup,
may ten thousand years be hard to exceed."
The ministers on the terrace were greatly pleased and laughed,
but the King of Yuè's face showed no joy.
Fàn Lǐ knew that Gōu Jiàn loved land,
and would not begrudge the death of his ministers;
seeing that his plans had succeeded and the state was settled,
he would surely return to his state without further need for merit,
hence his worried expression and lack of joy.
Fàn Lǐ, wishing to leave from Wú,
feared that if Gōu Jiàn had not yet returned,
it would betray the duty of a minister,
so he followed him into Yuè.
On the way, he said to Wén Zhǒng:
"You should leave now;
the King of Yuè will certainly execute you."
Zhǒng did not believe this.
Lǐ then sent a letter to Zhǒng, saying:
"I have heard that heaven has four seasons,
with spring giving life and winter bringing destruction.
Humans experience periods of prosperity and decline,
where great success inevitably leads to downfall.
To understand advancement and retreat, survival and perishation, without losing one's integrity,
is this not the mark of a wise person?
Although Lǐ lacks talent,
I clearly comprehend when to advance and retreat.
When the high-flying birds have scattered,
the fine bows will be stored away.
When the cunning rabbits have been exhausted,
the excellent hounds will be cooked.
Now, King Yuè has a long neck and beak-like mouth,
with the gaze of a hawk and the gait of a wolf.
He can be shared with during hardships but not in times of joy,
he can be accompanied through danger,
but not in peace.
If you do not leave,
he will bring harm upon you,
this is clear."
Wén Zhǒng did not believe his words.
The King of Yuè was scheming,
Fàn Lǐ proposed to leave,
seeking to escape misfortune.
In the twenty-fourth year,
on the ninth month, day Dīngwèi,
Fàn Lǐ bid farewell to the king, saying:
"Your servant has heard that when the ruler worries, the minister labors,
when the ruler is humiliated, the minister dies,
such is the unity of righteousness.
Now, in serving Your Majesty,
I failed to prevent disasters before they sprouted,
and later could not rescue already collapsing calamities.
Nevertheless,
I ultimately wished to help you establish a hegemon state,
thus I did not shirk from life or death,
I privately reflected,
and was sent to Wú.
The king's shame and humiliation,
the reason Lǐ did not die then,
was truly fearing slander from Grand Steward Pǐ,
leading to the fate of Wǔ Zǐxū.
Therefore, I dared not die beforehand,
but endured a little longer to survive.
The heart of shame cannot be great,
the sweat of humiliation cannot be endured.
Fortunately, relying on the spirits of the ancestral temple,
and Your Majesty's majestic virtue,
we turned defeat into success.
Just as Tāng and Wǔ overcame Xià and Shāng to achieve royal enterprise,
establishing merit and washing away shame,
is why I have remained in position so long.
I ask to take my leave now."
The King of Yuè was sorrowful,
tears falling and wetting his robes,
saying:
"The state's scholars and officials look to you,
the state's people look to you,
you made me entrust my body and title while awaiting destiny.
Now you speak of leaving,
wishing to depart.
This is heaven abandoning Yuè and bereaving me,
leaving me with nothing to rely on.
I privately have these words:
if you stay in office,
I will share the state with you;
if you leave,
your wife and children will be executed."
Fàn Lǐ replied:
"Your servant has heard that the nobleman awaits the right moment,
makes plans without frequent scheming,
dies without being suspected,
and does not deceive himself internally.
Since I am departing,
what law applies to my wife and children?
May Your Majesty strive on,
your servant bids farewell here."
Thereupon, he boarded a small boat,
exited the Three Rivers,
entered the Five Lakes,
and none knew where he went.
After Fàn Lǐ had left,
the King of Yuè turned pale with a changed expression,
summoned Minister Zhǒng and said:
"Can Lǐ be pursued?"
Zhǒng said:
"It is too late."
The king said:
"What can be done!"
Zhǒng said:
"When Lǐ left,
he drew six yin lines,
and three yang lines,
saying that the spirits of the day cannot restrain him,
the Dark Warrior and Heavenly Void exercise power,
who dares to stop him?
He passed the Heavenly Gate,
crossed the Heavenly Bridge,
then entered the Heavenly One,
with divine light shading his front.
Those who speak of it will die,
those who see it will go mad.
I wish Your Majesty would not pursue further.
Lǐ will never return."
The King of Yuè then gathered his wife and children,
enfeoffed them with a hundred lǐ of land,
declaring that anyone daring to invade them
would suffer heaven's calamity.
Thereupon,
the King of Yuè had skilled craftsmen cast a golden statue in Fàn Lǐ's likeness,
placed it beside his seat,
and discussed governance with it morning and night.
From then on,
Jì Nǎo feigned madness.
Ministers like Yè Yōng, Fú Tóng, and Gāo Rú
grew increasingly distant,
no longer intimate at court.
Minister Zhǒng, troubled internally, did not attend court,
and some slandered him to the king, saying:
"Wén Zhǒng abandoned his position as prime minister,
yet enabled Your Majesty to become hegemon among the feudal lords,
now his office is not increased,
his rank not further enfeoffed,
thus he harbors a resentful heart,
with anger boiling inside,
and changing countenance outwardly,
hence he does not attend court."
Another day,
Zhǒng remonstrated, saying:
"The reason I come to court early and leave late as if personally afflicted
was only for Wú's sake.
Now that it is destroyed,
what worries Your Majesty?"
The King of Yuè remained silent.
At that time, Duke Āi of Lǔ was troubled by the Three Huán families,
and wanted to use the feudal lords to attack them.
The Three Huán families also feared Duke Āi's anger,
thus ruler and minister created difficulties for each other.
Duke Āi fled to Xíng,
and the Three Huán attacked Duke Āi.
The duke fled to Wèi,
then fled to Yuè.
The state of Lǔ was left empty,
its people grieving,
came to welcome Duke Āi,
and returned together with him.
Gōu Jiàn was worried that Wén Zhǒng had no plans,
therefore he did not attack the Three Huán for Duke Āi.
In the twenty-fifth year,
at dawn on the bǐngwǔ day,
King Gōujiàn of Yuè summoned his Chancellor, the Grand Master Wén Zhǒng, and asked him:
"I have heard that knowing others is easy,
but knowing oneself is difficult.
What kind of person do you think the Chancellor is?"
Zhǒng replied:
"Alas,
Your Majesty knows my courage,
but not my benevolence.
You know my loyalty,
but not my trustworthiness.
I have indeed repeatedly reduced sensual pleasures,
eliminated excessive entertainments,
and with unconventional arguments and strange discourses,
exhausted my words and loyalty,
to confront Your Majesty,
going against your heart and offending your ears,
inevitably incurring guilt.
I dare not cherish life and remain silent,
but to speak and then die,
as Wǔ Zǐxū did in Wú in the past.
When Fūchāi was about to execute him,
he said to me:
'When the cunning hare is dead,
the good hound is cooked.
When the enemy state is destroyed,
the strategist minister perishes.'
Fàn Lǐ also had such words.
Why does Your Majesty ask about violating the eighth of the Yùmén?
I see Your Majesty's intent."
The King of Yuè remained silent and did not respond,
and the Grand Master also withdrew.
He was fed others' slanders as if they were truths.
His wife said:
"You are base!
As the Chancellor of a state,
do you lack the king's emoluments?
When dining, it's not enjoyed,
but fed with slander—why?
With wife and children by your side,
like a common man's abilities.
You have become Chancellor on your own,
what more do you hope for?
Is it not out of greed?
Why is your will so unsettled like this?"
Zhǒng said:
"How sorrowful,
you do not understand.
Since our king has escaped from calamities,
and avenged the disgrace against Wú,
I have moved my residence to throw myself into a place of death,
exhausted the strategies of the nine arts,
being cunning for him,
and loyal to the ruler,
yet the king does not discern it.
Instead, he says:
'Knowing others is easy,
but knowing oneself is difficult.'
I answered him, and he had no other words,
which is an omen of ill fortune.
I am about to go in again,
fearing I may not return,
bidding you a long farewell,
to seek each other in the netherworld."
His wife said:
"How do you know this?"
Zhǒng said:
"When I saw the king,
it was exactly the eighth violation of the Yùmén.
The hour overcoming the day,
the superior harming the inferior,
this signifies chaos and disgrace,
and will certainly harm the good.
Today the day overcomes the hour,
the superior's harm to the inferior ceases,
my life is but a moment away."
The King of Yuè again summoned the Chancellor,
and said to him:
"You possess secret strategies and military tactics,
to overthrow enemies and seize states.
Of the strategies of the nine arts,
three have been used now,
and the powerful Wú has already been defeated,
the remaining six are still with you.
I hope you will use the remaining arts to plan for my predecessor king underground against Wú's ancestors."
Thereupon, Zhǒng looked up to the sky and sighed:
"Alas!
I have heard that great kindness unrequited,
and great achievements unrewarded,
is this what it means?
I regret not following Fàn Lǐ's advice,
and thus being executed by the King of Yuè.
I did not heed good words,
so I was fed others' slanders."
The King of Yuè then bestowed upon Wén Zhǒng the sword Shǔlú.
Zhǒng received the sword,
and sighed again:
"The governor of Nányáng, yet captured by the King of Yuè."
He laughed at himself and said:
"At the end of a hundred generations,
loyal ministers will surely use me as an example."
Then he fell on the sword and died.
The King of Yuè buried Zhǒng in the Western Hills of the state,
with over three thousand naval soldiers,
constructing a tri-legged tomb passage,
some entering beneath the three peaks.
A year after the burial,
Wǔ Zǐxū came from the sea, pierced the mountain's flank, and took Zhǒng away,
floating together with him on the sea.
Thus, the one who awaits in the rising tide,
is Wǔ Zǐxū.
The one in the following heavy waters,
is Grand Master Zhǒng.
After the King of Yuè had executed the loyal minister,
he became hegemon east of the passes,
building a viewing tower from Lángyá,
the tower spanning seven lǐ in circumference,
to gaze upon the Eastern Sea,
with eight thousand death-defying warriors,
and three hundred spear boats.
Not long after,
he personally sought worthy scholars.
Confucius heard of this,
and followed by his disciples, presented the previous kings' refined qin and ritual music to Yuè.
The King of Yuè then donned the Tángyí armor,
girded the Bùguāng sword,
and held the Qūlú spear,
deploying three hundred death-defying warriors to form a阵 at the pass.
Confucius arrived in Yuè shortly after,
and the King of Yuè said:
"Yes, yes,
what does the Master have to teach me?"
Confucius said:
"I can expound the ways of the Five Emperors and Three Kings,
hence I present the refined qin to offer to Your Majesty."
The King of Yuè sighed deeply and said:
"The nature of Yuè people is brittle and foolish,
living on water and dwelling in mountains,
using boats as chariots,
oars as horses,
coming as if floating,
leaving hard to follow,
delighting in arms and daring death,
is the constant nature of Yuè.
What does the Master wish to teach them?"
Confucius did not answer,
but took his leave and departed.
The King of Yuè sent men to the Mùkè Mountain,
to retrieve Yǔncháng's remains,
intending to relocate the burial to Lángyá.
Three times they pierced Yǔncháng's tomb,
and each time, a blazing wind arose within the tomb, flying sand and stones to shoot at the people,
so that none could enter.
Gōujiàn said:
"Does my former lord not wish to be moved?"
So he abandoned the effort and left.
Gōujiàn then sent envoys to order Qí, Chǔ, Qín, and Jìn,
to all support the Zhōu court,
and after a blood oath, they departed.
Duke Huán of Qín did not comply with the King of Yuè's command,
so Gōujiàn selected officers and soldiers from Wú and Yuè,
crossed the river westward to attack Qín.
The troops suffered hardships.
Just as Qín became terrified,
admitting fault on their own,
Yuè then withdrew the army.
The soldiers were joyful,
and thus composed the poem "The River Bridge",
which said:
"Cross the river bridge, oh cross the river bridge,
raising troops to attack the King of Qín.
In early winter's tenth month, much snow and frost,
severe cold makes the road truly hard to bear.
Before the troops could cross, the Qín army surrendered,
all the lords were terrified and fearful.
Their fame spread across the seas, awing distant lands,
claiming hegemony like Mù, Huán, Qí, Chǔ, and Zhuāng.
Under heaven, peace and longevity reign,
sorrowful to leave, oh why no bridge to return."
Since Yuè destroyed Wú,
the Central States all feared it.
In the twenty-sixth year,
the King of Yuè captured the unruly Lord of Zhū and brought him back,
establishing his crown prince Hé in his place.
In winter,
Duke Āi of Lǔ, pressured by the Three Huán, fled to Yuè.
The King of Yuè wished to attack the Three Huán for him,
but because the lords and grand masters did not obey orders,
it did not come to fruition.
In the twenty-seventh year,
winter,
Gōu Jiàn fell seriously ill,
and as he was about to die,
he said to Crown Prince Xīng Yí:
"I, as a descendant of Yǔ,
inheriting the virtue of Yǔn Cháng,
blessed by the heavenly spirits and the favor of the gods,
from the barren land of Yuè,
with the vanguard assistance of Chǔ,
destroyed the spears and shields of the King of Wú.
Crossing rivers and traversing Huái,
reaching the lands of Jìn and Qí,
my achievements and virtue stand lofty.
Having reached this point on my own,
how could one not be sincere?
For those who come after a hegemon,
it is difficult to maintain long,
be cautious of this!"
Then he passed away.
Xīng Yí reigned for one year before his death,
succeeded by his son Wēng.
Wēng died,
succeeded by his son Bù Yáng.
Bù Yáng died,
succeeded by his son Wú Jiàng.
Wú Jiàng died,
succeeded by his son Yù.
Yù died,
succeeded by his son Zūn.
Zūn died,
succeeded by his son Qīn.
From Gōu Jiàn to Qīn,
there were eight rulers all claiming hegemony,
spanning 224 years.
Qīn lost all his followers,
and left Láng Yá,
moving to Wú.
From Huáng Dì to Shào Kāng,
ten generations.
From Yǔ receiving the throne to Shào Kāng's accession,
six generations,
covering 144 years.
